Stacked on https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/45 (`fm/xrpljs-submitandwait-outcomes-f14`) — review that one first; this PR's base is that branch.

## What was wrong

The integration harness never waited for a transaction to be validated. `testTransaction` read the preliminary code that `submit` returns — a prediction, not an outcome — asserted `tesSUCCESS` against it, and for an expected `tec*` code returned that same preliminary value, so a transaction that submitted `tesSUCCESS` and was validated `tecNO_PERMISSION` (or the reverse) passed unnoticed; nothing asserted `validated` anywhere. Meanwhile the CI `xrpld.cfg` omitted 11 amendments the `rippleci/xrpld:develop` image supports, `fixMPTDeliveredAmount` among them, so the suites silently ran without them; the unused `isAmendmentEnabled` helper would have reported every one of them off, because a standalone node applies `[features]` as rules in force from genesis without writing the ledger's `Amendments` object and therefore reports `enabled: false` for everything; and the integration README, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, the `xrpld.cfg` comments and `getNewAmendments.js` all described a container, an image and a `rippled.cfg` that CI does not use — the script crashed with `ENOENT` on the first line.

## What changed

**Validated outcomes (084)**
- `testTransaction` closes the ledger its transaction went into and then waits for it through `client.submitAndWait`, asserts `validated`, and asserts against the validated `meta.TransactionResult`. The return value is now a `TestTransactionResponse`: the `SubmitResponse` as before, plus `validatedResponse` (the `tx` response) and `finalResult` (the code the network actually recorded). Existing callers are unaffected — the type is a supertype of what they already read.
- An expected `errCode` of `tec*` is asserted against the validated result. `tem*`, `tef*`, `tel*` and `ter*` never reach a ledger, so those stay on the `submit` result, which is the only outcome they have.
- `verifySubmittedTransaction` asserts `result.validated`.

**Ledger progress (084)**
- `setupClient` closes a ledger every second in the background, which is what lets `submitAndWait` make progress against a node that otherwise only closes a ledger when asked. The ticker is `unref`'d and stopped by `teardownClient`.
- `setupClient(url, { closeLedgers: false })` opts out. `submitAndWait.test.ts` uses it: that suite asserts on exactly which ledger a transaction lands in and on how long a submission takes to settle.

**Amendments (021)**
- Added the 11 missing amendments to `[features]`: `fixAMMClawbackRounding`, `fixAMMv1_3`, `fixCleanup3_5_0`, `fixDirectoryLimit`, `fixEnforceNFTokenTrustlineV2`, `fixFillOrKill`, `fixIncludeKeyletFields`, `fixMPTDeliveredAmount`, `fixPayChanCancelAfter`, `fixPriceOracleOrder`, `fixTokenEscrowV1`.
- `setupClient` now fails, once per process and by name, when the node supports a non-retired amendment that `xrpld.cfg` does not list. Amendments the node reports as `vetoed: "Obsolete"` are retired — permanently in force and impossible to list — so they are skipped.

**Amendment detection (020)**
- `isAmendmentEnabled` takes a probe transaction and `simulate`s it, treating `temDISABLED` as "off", instead of reading `feature.enabled`. `test/integration/amendments.test.ts` covers it and pins the contradiction it exists for: MPTokensV1 is in force while `feature` reports it disabled.

**Documentation (019)**
- `test/integration/README.md` rewritten around the `rippleci/xrpld:develop` command CI actually runs, with the standalone node's three traps and the `PORT` override.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`: dropped the `validators.txt` that does not exist, and rewrote "Updating the Docker container for CI" — it named `/.ci-config/rippled.cfg` twice and described pasting amendment hashes.
- `.ci-config/xrpld.cfg`: the comment claiming `[features]` does not work in standalone mode said the opposite of the truth; replaced with what actually happens and why `feature` cannot be trusted. Also replaced the stale `WietseWind/docker-rippled` pointer and fixed the `Amednments` typo.
- `.ci-config/getNewAmendments.js`: read `xrpld.cfg` (it read `rippled.cfg`, which does not exist), ask the standalone node CI runs rather than devnet, and print amendment **names** rather than hashes to look up by hand. `XRPLD_WS_URL` overrides the node.

Findings covered: **019**, **020**, **021**, **084**.

The finding-062 scenario (validated in the last allowed ledger) is covered by `submitAndWait.test.ts`'s "returns a transaction validated in its last allowed ledger even when the validated ledger has moved past it", which arrives with the base branch.

## How it was tested

Against an own standalone node, `rippleci/xrpld:develop` published on 6124:

```
docker run --detach --publish 6124:6006 --volume "$PWD/.ci-config/:/etc/xrpld/" \
  --name xrpld-test-infra rippleci/xrpld:develop --standalone
```

| command | result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm run build` | exit 0 |
| `npm run lint` (root, `--max-warnings 0`) | 7 projects pass |
| `npx jest --config jest.config.unit.js` | 136 suites, 1362 tests pass |
| `PORT=6124 npx jest --config jest.config.integration.js --runInBand` | 102 suites, 220 tests pass |
| `XRPLD_WS_URL=ws://localhost:6124 node .ci-config/getNewAmendments.js` | `No new amendments to add!` |

The new setup assertion was verified by deleting `fixMPTDeliveredAmount` from `xrpld.cfg` and re-running: setup fails with `1 amendment(s) supported by the node under test are missing from .ci-config/xrpld.cfg: fixMPTDeliveredAmount.` The line was restored.

The container was removed with `docker rm -f xrpld-test-infra`.

## Follow-ups discovered (not fixed here)

1. **`submitAndWait` cannot wait on a blob that is only in the open ledger.** `handleTerminalSubmission` keeps polling for `tefALREADY` and looks the hash up for other `tef*` codes, but rippled answers `tefPAST_SEQ` — not `tefALREADY` — when the transaction is in the open ledger and not yet validated, so the lookup finds nothing and it throws. This is why `testTransaction` has to close a ledger before waiting. Worth handling in `packages/xrpl/src/sugar/submit.ts` (base branch's file).
2. **`FeatureAllResponse` has no `vetoed` field**, so distinguishing a retired amendment needs a cast. That is finding 032, another unit.
3. **A failing `beforeEach` is masked**: `afterEach` then throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined` on the undefined context, burying the real error. Pre-existing in every integration suite.
4. **`getNewAmendments.js` needs `npm run build` first**, since it `require`s the workspace `xrpl` package for its WebSocket client. Documented, not changed.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/26
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

body:
Stacked on #45 (`fm/xrpljs-submitandwait-outcomes-f14`) — review only the last commit; the base retargets to `main` once #45 merges.

Closes #5. Part of the MPT audit epic #2.

## Problem

Four audit findings, all on the path from a transaction object to its validated result. Each one throws the transaction type away at a different point, so the caller gets a union back and casts it away again.

**001 — `submitAndWait` types `meta` as `TransactionMetadata<T> | string | undefined`.** It reuses `TxResponse<T>`, the shape written for the raw `tx` RPC, where `meta` is optional (the transaction may be pending) and may be a hex string (`binary: true`). Neither can happen on this path: the sugar never sets `binary`, and it only returns once the lookup is `validated`. `!` does not help, because it strips `undefined` and leaves `string`:

```ts
const res = await client.submitAndWait(createTx, { wallet })
res.result.meta.TransactionResult
// TS2339: Property 'TransactionResult' does not exist on type
//   'string | TransactionMetadata<...> | undefined'.
```

**002 — `Wallet.sign` erases the transaction type.** `tx_blob` is a bare `string`, so `submitAndWait(tx_blob)` infers `T = SubmittableTransaction` and `meta` becomes the union of every special-cased metadata shape. The documented workaround, `submitAndWait<MPTokenIssuanceCreate>(tx_blob)`, is an assertion the compiler cannot check against the blob.

**030 — `simulate` does not thread the type through, and skips autofill's normalisation.** `SimulateJsonResponse<T>` already has the parameter; the client never supplied it. Worse, `simulate` sent the transaction as-is, so two things `submitAndWait` accepts were rejected by rippled:

```
RippledError: Field 'tx_json.Flags' has bad type.        // Flags: { tfMPTLock: true }
RippledError: Field 'tx_json.DeliverMax' is unknown.     // autofill folds DeliverMax into Amount
```

**033 — `autofill` returns its input type**, so `Sequence`, `Fee` and `LastLedgerSequence` are still optional after autofill has populated them, and the `Flags` union survives the conversion to a number.

## Fix

Type-only except for `simulate`'s request normalisation.

- **`TxResponse<T, Binary>`** gains a `Binary` parameter, defaulting to `boolean` so `meta` keeps both shapes for anyone who does not pin it down. New `ValidatedTxResponse<T>` = `TxResponse<T, false>` with `meta: TransactionMetadata<T>` and `validated: true`; `submitAndWait`, `waitForFinalTransactionOutcome` and `handleTerminalSubmission` return it.
- The two `as TxResponse<T>` casts in `sugar/submit.ts` — one carrying `// TODO: resolve the type assertion below` — are replaced by `asValidatedTxResponse`, which checks `validated` **and** that `meta` is decoded before narrowing. Only the caller-supplied `T` stays an assertion, since no runtime check can confirm it. A lookup that is validated but carries a hex `meta` is now treated as "not final yet" rather than returned as if it were decoded.
- **`SignedBlob<T>`** (`string & { readonly __xrplTx?: T }`) is returned by a now-generic `Wallet.sign`. The brand is an optional phantom property that is never populated, so a `SignedBlob` is a plain string at runtime and assignable to `string`; `submitAndWait` and `simulate` take `T | SignedBlob<T> | string` and infer `T` from it, still falling back to the union for a plain string.
- **`simulate<T, Binary>`** returns `SimulateJsonResponse<T>` and routes the transaction through `normalizeForSimulate` — the part of `autofill` that needs no network: `convertTxFlagsToNumber` plus `handleDeliverMax`. It works on a copy, so the caller's object is untouched. Nothing that needs a round trip (`Sequence`, `Fee`, `LastLedgerSequence`) is filled in; `simulate` does not require those.
- **`Autofilled<T>`** = `T & { Sequence: number; Fee: string; LastLedgerSequence: number; Flags?: number }`, returned by `autofill`. The intersection is assignable to `T`, so no existing caller widens. Ticket users keep `Sequence: 0`, which still satisfies `number`.

## Compatibility

Non-breaking for values: every new type is assignable where the old one was, and the runtime shapes are unchanged apart from `simulate`'s normalisation. One source-level break: `simulate`'s first type parameter is now `T`, so an explicit `client.simulate<true>(tx)` becomes `client.simulate<MyTx, true>(tx)`. No call site in this repo did that.

## Tests

- `packages/xrpl/test/client/submitPathTypes.test.ts` (new, 6 cases) — the typed assignments are the assertions, paired with runtime checks. Red before this commit with exactly the errors the findings quote (`Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'MPTokenIssuanceCreateMetadata'`, `Type 'boolean | undefined' is not assignable to type 'true'`, `'"../../src"' has no exported member 'Autofilled' / 'SignedBlob'`, `Type 'unknown' is not assignable to type 'string'` for `tx_json.MPTokenIssuanceID`); green after.
- `packages/xrpl/test/integration/requests/simulate.test.ts` — two new cases for the only runtime change. Against a standalone `rippleci/xrpld:develop` node they fail before with `Field 'tx_json.Flags' has bad type.` and `Field 'tx_json.DeliverMax' is unknown.`, and pass after (all 5 cases in the file green).
- `packages/xrpl/test/integration/submitAndWait.test.ts` — `autofilled.Sequence ?? 1` dropped; `Sequence` is no longer optional, and lint flags the dead `??`.

Checks run: `npm run build`, `npm test` in `packages/xrpl` (137 suites, 1368 tests), root `npm run lint`, `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json`, and `tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.eslint.json --target es2020` for the test tree.

## Follow-ups (out of scope here)

- The 18 `as TransactionMetadata` casts in `test/integration` that finding 001 counts all sit on raw `client.request({ command: 'tx' })` lookups, not on `submitAndWait`, so this change does not remove them. Most of them re-fetch a transaction `testTransaction` already returned; collapsing them onto the `submitAndWait` result would drop both the round trip and the cast.
- `MPTokenIssuanceCreateMetadata` and the other per-transaction metadata interfaces are not re-exported from the package root, so the new unit test imports it by path.
- `TxV1Response` did not get the `Binary` parameter; the v1 `tx` shape is untouched here.
- Finding 030 also suggested an `autofill?: boolean` option on `simulate` for callers that want the full network-backed autofill. Not added: nothing on the simulate path needs `Sequence`/`Fee`, and it would turn a single request into several.
- `simulate` still does not convert X-addresses (`setValidAddresses`), which `autofill` does.
title: fix(xrpl): keep the transaction type through sign, autofill, simulate and submitAndWait

body:
Stacked on https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/33 (`fm/xrpljs-mpt-ledger-types-f01`) — this PR is based on that branch, so review only the commits after it.

It also carries the commits of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/38 (`fm/xrpljs-rpc-additions-f20`), merged in so the two branches' `HISTORY.md` sections combine cleanly; they drop out once that PR merges.

## What was wrong

Building an MPT with clawback, pre-emptive banning and freeze meant hand-rolling almost every identifier the flow needs. The MPTokenIssuanceID (32-bit consumed sequence ‖ 20-byte issuer AccountID) had to be assembled by hand, and the ticketed case got it wrong — the ID uses the sequence the `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` *consumed*, i.e. `TicketSequence` when a ticket was used, not the `Sequence` of `0`. The `MPTokenIssuance`, `MPToken`, `Credential` and `PermissionedDomain` ledger indexes had no keylet helpers at all, even though the `Credential` and `PermissionedDomain` indexes are the `CredentialID`/`DomainID` that the MPT compliance transactions take as inputs. `MPTAmount.value` is the integer unit count, so an issuance with `AssetScale: 2` needed a by-hand `× 100` at every call site. The MPT `TransferFee` is in 0.001% increments, unlike the billionths `TransferRate`, so `percentToTransferRate` silently produces a wrong (and out-of-range) fee — and `MAX_TRANSFER_FEE` was not exported to check against. The only typed reads of an `MPTokenIssuance`/`MPToken` lived in the confidential module, where nobody doing plain MPT work would look, and a transaction object literal widens its `TransactionType` to `string`, so every hand-built transaction needed an `as Payment`-style assertion that also silences real field errors.

## What changed

All new symbols are exported from the package root.

**MPTokenIssuanceID** (`src/utils/getMPTokenIssuanceID.ts`)
* `getMPTokenIssuanceID(tx)` / `getMPTokenIssuanceID(issuer, sequence)` — uses `TicketSequence ?? Sequence`, accepts an X-address, and validates the sequence is a uint32. The ID is known before submission, once `autofill` has assigned a sequence.
* `parseMPTokenIssuanceID(id)` → `{ sequence, issuer }`.
* `getMPTokenIssuanceIDFromMeta(meta)` — prefers rippled's synthetic `mpt_issuance_id`, falls back to deriving from the created node (so it also works on binary metadata), and returns `undefined` unless `TransactionResult === 'tesSUCCESS'`.

**Keylets** (`src/utils/hashes/`)
* `hashMPTokenIssuance`, `hashMPToken`, `hashCredential`, `hashPermissionedDomain`, plus the four missing `ledgerSpaces` entries (`~`, `t`, `D`, `m`). `hashMPToken` hashes the **32-byte issuance ledger index**, not the 24-byte ID, matching rippled's `keylet::mptoken`.
* `getCreatedEntryIndex(meta, ledgerEntryType)` for the index of any entry a transaction created, for the cases with no computable keylet and no synthetic ID.

**AssetScale** (`src/utils/mptConversion.ts`)
* `mptToUnits('12.34', 2) === '1234'` and `unitsToMpt('1234', 2) === '12.34'` — the MPT analogues of `xrpToDrops`/`dropsToXrp`, bounded by `MAX_MPT_AMOUNT` and string-valued so 2^63−1 survives.

**TransferFee** (`src/utils/quality.ts`, `MPTokenIssuanceCreate.ts`)
* `percentToMPTTransferFee('1%') === 1000`, `mptTransferFeeToPercent(500) === '0.5'`, and `MAX_MPT_TRANSFER_FEE`. `MAX_TRANSFER_FEE` is now exported, has a doc comment, and the `TransferFee` field documents that it is *not* a `TransferRate`.

**Read helpers** (`src/utils/mptLedgerEntries.ts`)
* `fetchMPToken` and `fetchMPTokenIssuance` moved out of `src/confidential/ledger.ts` (which re-exports them, so existing deep imports keep working) and now take `MPTLedgerReader` — anything with a `request` method — rather than a whole `Client`.
* `fetchMPTokenOrUndefined` / `fetchMPTokenIssuanceOrUndefined` return `undefined` on `entryNotFound` and rethrow anything else, so "does this account hold the token?" needs no try/catch.

**Typed factory** (`src/models/transactions/transactionFactory.ts`)
* `tx(literal)` returns the literal at its narrow union-member type, and `TransactionOf<'MPTokenIssuanceCreate'>` names that type. No assertion, and a misspelled field is still an error.

Also: a `HISTORY.md` entry under Unreleased and an MPT line in the README feature list.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/21
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

### Findings covered

012, 082, 083, 016 (the `AssetScale` helper half), 080, 003.

## How it was tested

Expected IDs and ledger indexes in the tests were captured from a standalone `rippled` (`rippleci/xrpld:develop`, `--standalone`) by actually creating an MPT issuance (plain and ticketed), an `MPToken`, a `Credential` and a `PermissionedDomain`, and reading back the `LedgerIndex` rippled assigned. The container was removed afterwards.

* `npm run build` — exit 0 (7 projects).
* `packages/xrpl` `npm test` — 140 suites, 1413 tests, all passing. New suites: `test/utils/getMPTokenIssuanceID.test.ts`, `test/utils/mptConversion.test.ts`, `test/utils/getCreatedEntryIndex.test.ts`, `test/utils/mptLedgerEntries.test.ts`, `test/models/transactionFactory.test.ts`, plus new cases in `test/utils/hashes.test.ts` and `test/utils/transferRate.test.ts`.
* `npm run lint` (root, `--max-warnings 0`) — exit 0.
* `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json` — exit 0.
* The `tx()` test was verified to be a real check: the same literal bound to a plain `const` and assigned to `Payment` fails with `TS2322: Type '{ TransactionType: string; ... }' is not assignable to type 'Payment'`.
* The `mptTransferFeeToPercent` test caught a real scale bug during development (dividing by 100000 instead of 1000), which is fixed here.

No integration test: nothing in this PR changes what is submitted to a ledger.

## Follow-ups discovered

* `MPTAmount.value` is still not validated as a non-negative integer string within `MAX_MPT_AMOUNT` — that validator tightening is finding 016's other half and belongs to the `mpt-validators` unit (https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/47), so it is deliberately not touched here.
* `getMPTokenIssuanceID` takes a `string | MPTokenIssuanceIDSource` union rather than overloads, because the repo's `jsdoc/check-param-names` rule cannot express an overload set. A caller passing an address and forgetting the sequence gets a `ValidationError` at runtime instead of a compile error.
* `hashCredential` and `hashPermissionedDomain` are not MPT-specific but live in the MPT unit because the MPT compliance flow is what needs them; a broader sweep of missing keylets (`Check`, `DepositPreauth`, `Ticket`, ...) would be a natural follow-up.
* `confidential/index.ts` no longer lists `fetchMPToken`/`fetchMPTokenIssuance` in its export block (they would collide at the package root with the `utils` exports of the same functions). They are the same functions, reachable from the root and from `confidential/ledger.ts`.

body:
Stacked on https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/33 (`fm/xrpljs-mpt-ledger-types-f01`) — base this PR on that branch; review only the second commit.

## What was wrong

Every read path in the client returned the widest possible type, so the request you wrote told the type system nothing about the response you got back. `ledger_entry` typed `result.node` as the whole `LedgerEntry` union even when the request carried `mpt_issuance: <id>` and could only ever return an `MPTokenIssuance`; `account_objects` typed `result.account_objects` as `AccountObject[]` even with `type: 'mpt_issuance'`; `TransactionStream` and `AccountTxTransaction` typed `meta` as the base `TransactionMetadata` with no relationship to the `tx_json` sitting next to it, so the synthetic `meta.mpt_issuance_id` that rippled returns on an `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` was simply not reachable; and `client.request` always returned the v2 response shape even when the request said `api_version: 1`, so v1 callers were told the fields were at `result.tx_json` when rippled puts them at the top level of `result`. In every case the caller's only recourse was an `as` cast — the diff removes 20-odd of them from this repo's own integration tests, which is the clearest measure of how often users were paying that tax.

## What changed

- **`ledger_entry` (005).** New `LedgerEntryLookupMap` maps each lookup field to its entry type, and `LedgerEntryNode<T>` resolves the request to a node type. A request with exactly one required mapped lookup field narrows (`mpt_issuance` → `MPTokenIssuance`, `mptoken` → `MPToken`, `account_root` → `AccountRoot`, `bridge` → `Bridge`, ...). A request using `index`, one with no mapped field, or one whose mapped field is a union falls back to the full `LedgerEntry` union, so nothing that compiled before stops compiling. Binary lookups are untouched and still yield `node_binary`.
- **`account_objects` (007).** New `AccountObjectByFilter` maps all 28 `AccountObjectType` filters to their entry types; `AccountObjectsResponse` gained an optional type parameter defaulting to `AccountObject`, and `AccountObjectsResponseMap<T>` picks the element type from the request's `type`. Wired into `RequestResponseMap`, `RequestAllResponseMap` and `RequestNextPageReturnMap`, so `requestAll` and `requestNextPage` narrow identically. Without a `type` filter the union is unchanged.
- **`meta` ↔ `tx_json` correlation (058).** `TransactionStream<T>`, `TransactionV1Stream<T>` and `AccountTxTransaction<Version, T>` now take the transaction type, defaulting to `Transaction`, and thread it through `meta: TransactionMetadata<T>` and `tx_json`/`tx`/`transaction`. `TransactionMetadata<T>` was already a conditional map, so `TransactionStream<MPTokenIssuanceCreate>['meta']` is `MPTokenIssuanceCreateMetadata` and `meta.mpt_issuance_id` type-checks.
- **`api_version` (078).** `BaseRequest.api_version` is now `APIVersion` (`1 | 2`) instead of `number`, and its doc comment no longer claims the default is version 1. New `RequestAPIVersion<T>` reads a literal `api_version` off the request; `Client.request` and `Client.requestAll` use it as the *default* for their version type parameter, so `request({ command: 'tx', ..., api_version: 1 })` returns `TxV1Response` while explicit call sites like `request<TxRequest, 1>(...)` keep working unchanged. `Client.apiVersion`'s doc comment now says plainly that it changes the runtime shape but not the static type, and that `api_version` belongs on the request if you want the types to follow.

### Deviation from the finding's proposed fix (058)

Finding 058 proposed a distributed union — `TxWithMeta<T> = { tx_json: T; meta: TransactionMetadata<T> }` over every member of `Transaction` — so that checking `ev.tx_json.TransactionType` would narrow `ev.meta`. I built it and it does not work: TypeScript does not narrow a parent object through a discriminant on a *nested* property, so `if (ev.tx_json?.TransactionType === 'MPTokenIssuanceCreate') { ev.meta?.mpt_issuance_id }` still fails with TS2339 under that shape. The union would have paid a large instantiation cost for no narrowing. The generic parameter reaches the same goal, and the supported idiom is a one-line user-defined type predicate:

```ts
function isIssuanceCreate(
  ev: TransactionStream,
): ev is TransactionStream<MPTokenIssuanceCreate> {
  return ev.tx_json?.TransactionType === 'MPTokenIssuanceCreate'
}
```

which the new unit test exercises end to end. Callers who already know the transaction type (the common case — you subscribed because you sent it) can just annotate `TransactionStream<MPTokenIssuanceCreate>` directly.

## Findings covered

- 005 — `ledger_entry` does not narrow `result.node` by lookup field
- 007 — `account_objects` does not narrow by `type` filter
- 058 — `meta` is not correlated with the transaction in streams and `account_tx`
- 078 — `api_version` on the request does not select the response type

## How this was tested

The fork has GitHub Actions disabled, so local checks are the gate. All run from the repo root unless noted, on top of `fm/xrpljs-mpt-ledger-types-f01`:

| Command | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `npm ci` | exit 0 |
| `npm run build` | exit 0 — 7 projects |
| `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json` | exit 0 |
| `npx tsc --noEmit --target es2020 -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.eslint.json` (src + tests) | exit 0 |
| `npm test` in `packages/xrpl` | 136 suites, 1360 tests, all passing |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0 — 7 projects, `--max-warnings 0` |

New unit test `packages/xrpl/test/models/responseNarrowing.test.ts` (14 tests) asserts the narrowing at both the type level (a `typeIs<Equals<A, B>>()` helper, plus `@ts-expect-error` on fields that must *not* resolve) and the runtime level against `createMockRippled`. Red-before check: with `packages/xrpl/src` reverted and the test kept,

```
npx jest --no-cache --config=jest.config.unit.js --coverage=false test/models/responseNarrowing.test.ts
```

fails to compile with the expected errors for all four findings — `Property 'mpt_issuance_id' does not exist on type 'AccountObject'`, `Property 'mpt_issuance_id' does not exist on type 'TransactionMetadata'`, `Type 'TransactionStream' is not generic`, `Property 'Account' does not exist on type 'BaseTxResult<2, Transaction> & { tx_json: Transaction; }'`. (`--no-cache` is required — ts-jest otherwise replays the compiled output from the green run.) With `src` restored it is green again.

No integration test was added or run: this change is type-level only, with no change to any request sent or response parsed at runtime.

The integration-test churn in this PR is a consequence, not a drive-by: once the narrowing lands, ~20 `as SomeLedgerEntry` casts and two `LedgerEntryType === '...'` guards become provably redundant, and `@typescript-eslint/no-unnecessary-type-assertion` / `no-unnecessary-condition` fail the lint gate until they are removed. Those deletions are the most direct evidence the fix does what it claims.

## Follow-ups discovered (not fixed here)

- **`BaseTransaction extends Record<string, unknown>`** (`packages/xrpl/src/models/transactions/common.ts:670`) defeats all property checking on transaction types: `payment.tx_json` type-checks on a `Payment`, and so does any typo. It also silently weakens the `api_version: 1` narrowing in this PR — `TxV1Response['result']` accepts any key because it intersects the transaction. Dropping that index signature is a breaking change and belongs in its own unit; it appears to be what https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/46 targets.
- **`LedgerEntryFilter` vs the `ledger_entry` lookup fields.** `ledger_entry` accepts lookup fields (`amendments`, `fee`, `hashes`, `nft_offer`, `oracle`, `permissioned_domain`, `signer_list`, `vault`, `loan`, `loan_broker`) that have no entry in `LedgerEntryLookupMap` yet, so they still fall back to the union. Filling those in is additive and safe; I kept the map to the entries the audit covers to keep this diff reviewable.
- **`bridge_account` is deliberately not in the lookup map.** A bridge lookup sets both `bridge_account` and `bridge`; mapping only `bridge` keeps "exactly one mapped lookup field" true and resolves to `Bridge`. If more multi-field lookups appear, the single-key rule in `LedgerEntryNode` will need revisiting.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/4
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Stacked on https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/40 (base branch `fm/xrpljs-autofill-tickets-and-batch-sequences-f15`) — review that one first; this diff is only the last commit.

Findings 090, 102, 103, 104, 105, 106 of the MPT audit, all in the XLS-56 Batch co-signing path.

## What was wrong

- **090** — `signMultiBatch` built its required-signer set from the inner `Account`/`Delegate` only. The `Sponsor` of a sponsored inner transaction (XLS-68) authorizes it with a `BatchSigners` entry — the inner `SponsorSignature` is only an empty placeholder — so there was no way to produce a sponsored Batch: `signMultiBatch(sponsorWallet, batch)` threw "Must be signing for an address submitting a transaction in the Batch."
- **102** — `combineBatchSigners` kept one `BatchSigner` fragment per account. Two co-signers of one multi-signed account each produce a fragment with their own `Signers[]`; combining them silently discarded all but one, so the account never reached its SignerList quorum. `signMultiBatch` had the same shape of bug in the small: it assigned `transaction.BatchSigners = [...]`, overwriting whatever was already there, so co-signing one Batch object twice lost the first signature.
- **103** — `signMultiBatch` had no precondition. The signature binds the outer sequence value and every inner transaction hash, so signing before `Client.autofill` bound `Sequence: 0` and hashes of inner transactions that had no `Sequence`/`Fee` yet; the Batch then failed on-ledger with no hint as to why. `Client.submit` made it worse by autofilling a co-signed Batch on the way out, changing those same fields after they were signed.
- **104** — rippled rejects the Batch `Account` as a `BatchSigner` with `temBAD_SIGNER`. `signMultiBatch` and `validate()` both accepted it, and only `combineBatchSigners` removed it — silently, so nobody learned the fragment was wrong, and a hand-built or single-fragment submission still hit `temBAD_SIGNER`.
- **105** — there was no way to check a `BatchSigner` co-signature before combining or submitting fragments received from other parties. `BatchSigners` is a non-signing field, so the outer `TxnSignature` does not cover it, yet `verifySignature` returned `true` for a correctly outer-signed Batch whose `BatchSigners` were garbage.
- **106** — `combineBatchSigners`' doc said it returned "the combined transaction, signed". The result is unsigned: `BatchSigners` is not the outer signature.

## What changed

`packages/xrpl/src/Wallet/batchSigner.ts`

- `signMultiBatch` adds the inner `Sponsor` (and `Counterparty`) to the involved-account set (090); throws when `batchAccount` is the Batch `Account`, naming `Wallet.sign` as the right tool (104); throws a `ValidationError` listing the missing fields when the Batch is not autofilled — outer `Sequence`/`TicketSequence`, inner `Sequence`, `Fee`, `SigningPubKey` (103); and merges its new entry into the existing `BatchSigners` instead of replacing them (102).
- `combineBatchSigners` merges fragments per account: multi-signed entries pool their `Signers` (de-duplicated by `Signer.Account`, sorted with `compareSigners`), identical single signatures collapse, and conflicting or mixed single/multi entries throw instead of silently losing a signature (102). It no longer strips a `BatchSigner` for the Batch `Account` — `validateBatch` now rejects that loudly (104). Doc corrected to state the result is unsigned and to spell out the order: autofill → co-sign → combine → outer sign → submit with `autofill: false` (106).
- New `verifyBatchSigners(batch)` returns `{ account, valid }` per entry, checking single and multi-signed entries against the XLS-56 V1_1 payload, and works on unsigned fragments (105). Exported from `src/Wallet/index.ts` along with `BatchSignerVerification`.
- The payload encoder is now one shared helper (`encodeBatchSignerPayload`), used by signing, verification and the equivalence key, so the three can't drift.

`packages/xrpl/src/models/transactions/batch.ts` — `validateBatch` rejects a `BatchSigners` entry whose `Account` is the Batch `Account` (104).

`packages/xrpl/src/Wallet/signer.ts` — `verifySignature` (so also `Wallet.verifyTransaction`) requires every `BatchSigner` of a Batch to verify (105).

`packages/xrpl/src/sugar/submit.ts` — `getSignedTx` compares the signature-bound fields before and after `autofill` and throws if a co-signed Batch would be changed, pointing at `autofill: false` (103).

## How tested

From `packages/xrpl`:

- `npm test` → `Test Suites: 134 passed`, `Tests: 1366 passed`.
- New unit tests: `test/wallet/batchSigner.test.ts` (31 tests — sponsor signing, appending a second signature, pooling two multisign `Signers`, rejecting the Batch `Account`, the un-autofilled error naming the missing fields, merging multisign fragments through `combineBatchSigners`, and a `verifyBatchSigners` block covering tampered signatures, a mutated inner transaction, missing signature material and non-Batch input), `test/models/batch.test.ts` (Batch `Account` as `BatchSigner`), `test/wallet/signer.test.ts` (`verifySignature` false on a Batch with a tampered `BatchSigner`), `test/client/submit.test.ts` (submit throws when autofill would invalidate the co-signatures, and succeeds with `autofill: false`).
- Red-before/green-after: with the five source files reverted (`git checkout --`) and `npx jest --no-cache`, the four suites gave `Test Suites: 4 failed` / `Tests: 3 failed` (the `batchSigner` suite cannot even compile without `verifyBatchSigners`); restored, all 60 pass.
- `npm run lint` → exit 0. `npm run build` → exit 0.
- Integration against standalone rippled (`rippleci/xrpld:develop`, own container on port 6116): `PORT=6116 npx jest --config=jest.config.integration.js test/integration/transactions/batch.test.ts` → `Tests: 3 passed`, including a new `batch with two co-signers combined` case that autofills once, has two accounts co-sign separate fragments, combines them, asserts both verify, and submits the merged Batch successfully. `payment.test.ts` also re-run green (5 passed) as a submit-path sanity check.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- `signMultiBatch` cannot produce a `BatchSigner` for an account that signs with a regular key *and* wants `Signers`-style multisign under a different signing account than the wallet address; the `multisign: string` overload conflates "signer account" with "regular key holder".
- `combineBatchSigners` still has no way to report *which* fragment was bad when equivalence fails — it only says the account/sequence/flags/hashes differ.
- `verifyBatchSigners` does not check quorum: it says each `Signer` signature is valid, not that the account's SignerList quorum is met (that needs a ledger lookup, so it belongs on `Client`).
- The inner `SponsorSignature` placeholder is not validated as empty on an inner Batch transaction.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/18
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/8
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Audit findings: **055** (the `BaseRequest` index signature half) and **026**.

## What was wrong

**055.** `BaseRequest` declared `[x: string]: unknown`. Every request type extends it, so every key on every request was optional and untyped. rippled ignores keys it does not recognise, so a misspelled key compiled and then silently did the wrong thing:

```ts
await client.request({
  command: 'ledger_entry',
  mpt_issuance: id,
  ledger_indx: 'validated',   // typo: read the *current* ledger instead
})

await client.request({
  command: 'account_objects',
  account: addr,
  typ: 'mptoken',             // typo: returned *every* object type
})
```

Both compiled cleanly before this PR. For an MPT issuer these are the difference between reading a frozen state and reading an unvalidated one, and between listing the MPTokens you asked for and listing everything the account owns.

**026.** The `Request` union had no admin commands, so `ledger_accept` had no type. The repo worked around this in its own integration harness by dropping to the private transport:

```ts
export async function sendLedgerAccept(client: Client): Promise<unknown> {
  return client.connection.request({ command: 'ledger_accept' })
}
```

`client.connection` is not public API, and the result was `unknown`.

## What changed

Removing the index signature is necessary but **not sufficient**. `Client.request` infers `R` from the request literal, and TypeScript does not apply excess-property checks to an inferred type parameter — so with the index signature simply deleted, the typos above still compile. `request` is now two overloads:

```ts
public async request<R extends Request, V extends APIVersion = ..., T = RequestResponseMap<R, V>>(
  req: StrictRequest<R>,
): Promise<T>

public async request<R extends BaseRequest, T extends BaseResponse = BaseResponse>(
  req: UnknownCommandRequest<R>,
): Promise<T>
```

- `StrictRequest<R>` types every key the matching `Request` member does not declare as `never`, which is what actually rejects the typo.
- `UnknownCommandRequest<R>` accepts a request **only** when its `command` is not in the `Request` union. Without that guard the fallback overload would happily swallow every typo on a known command. This is why a typo now surfaces as a `command: never` error — that message means "this literal has a key its request type does not declare", and it is called out in the doc comment and the changelog.

A `ledger_accept` request/response pair is added and wired into `Request`, `Response` and `RequestResponseMap`, and `sendLedgerAccept` now goes through public `client.request` and returns a typed `LedgerAcceptResponse`.

Requests with a command xrpl.js has no types for keep working, and can name their own response type:

```ts
await client.request({ command: 'log_level', severity: 'debug' })            // BaseResponse
await client.request<{ command: 'log_level'; severity: string }, LogLevelResponse>({ ... })
```

## BREAKING

`BaseRequest` no longer has an index signature, and `Client.request` rejects keys the command's request type does not declare.

- **A misspelled key is now a compile error.** It is reported as `command: never`. Fix the key.
- **To send a key xrpl.js does not know about yet** (a newly amended field), assert the literal to the command's request type — the key is still sent on the wire:
  ```ts
  client.request({ command: 'ledger_entry', loan: id } as LedgerEntryRequest)
  ```
- **Interfaces that extend `BaseRequest` to add their own keys must now declare each key.** They previously inherited the index signature.

## Latent bugs this caught

The type check turned up four real problems in this repo's own tests, all fixed here because the build has to be green:

| File | Problem |
| --- | --- |
| `test/integration/requests/getAggregatePrice.test.ts` | `account` is not a key of `GetAggregatePriceRequest` — sent and ignored |
| `test/integration/requests/ripplePathFind.test.ts` | `subcommand: 'create'` belongs to `path_find`, not `ripple_path_find` — sent and ignored |
| `test/connection.test.ts` | stale `@ts-expect-error` on `test_command`, now typed by the fallback overload |
| `test/client/subscribe.test.ts` | `// @es-expect-error` — a typo'd directive that never suppressed anything (see follow-ups) |

## How this was tested

Red before, green after — with the index signature restored, all three typo assertions report `TS2578: Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive`, i.e. the typos compiled.

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.eslint.json --target es2020` — clean (src + tests)
- `npm test` in `packages/xrpl` — **134 suites, 1343 tests, all passing**
- `npm run lint` at the root (`--max-warnings 0`) — clean across all 7 packages
- `npm run build` at the root — clean

New unit tests in `test/client/request.test.ts` cover `ledger_accept`, an unknown command resolving to `BaseResponse`, an unknown command with an explicit response type, and a never-called function whose three `@ts-expect-error` calls fail the suite if a misspelled key ever compiles again.

Integration tests were run because `sendLedgerAccept` — which the entire integration harness depends on — changed transport path from `client.connection.request` to `client.request`, and because two live request payloads changed. Against a standalone rippled on a dedicated port: **36 suites, 69 tests in `test/integration/requests`, all passing**.

This fork has GitHub Actions disabled, so local checks above are the gate.

## Follow-ups (not fixed here)

- **`manifestReceived` listeners are typed with a request type.** `OnEventToListenerMap` maps `'manifestReceived'` to `(manifest: ManifestRequest) => void`, but rippled sends the manifest *stream* message (the fixture at `test/fixtures/rippled/streams/manifest.json` has `type: 'manifestReceived'`, `master_key`, `seq`, …). The index signature hid this; the test at `subscribe.test.ts:140` carried a typo'd `// @es-expect-error` that never suppressed anything. A real `@ts-expect-error` plus this note replaces it. The fix is a `ManifestStream` type, which belongs with the stream shapes, not here.
- **The other half of finding 055** — the `LedgerEntryRequest` lookup members that are missing (`permissioned_domain`, `vault`, `oracle`, `nft_offer`, `loan`) — is owned by the `rpc-response-shapes` unit per `audit/PLAN.md`, and is untouched here.
- The type repros under `audit/` (`audit015and026`, the 055 typo lines) no longer compile now that this landed, which is the intended outcome. `audit/` belongs to the audit PR and is deliberately untouched.
title: fix(xrpl)!: reject request keys the command does not declare

Stacked on https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/33 (`fm/xrpljs-mpt-ledger-types-f01`) — review/merge that one first; this PR targets its branch and its diff will shrink to the last commit once that lands.

## What was wrong

`Client.getBalances` built its answer from `account_info` (XRP) and `account_lines` (trust lines) only, so an account's Multi-Purpose Token holdings were silently absent from the result — and the inline return type it declared had no field that could have expressed one, so a caller could not even work around it by reaching past the helper. `getBalanceChanges` had the mirror-image gap: its metadata walk handled `AccountRoot` and `RippleState` nodes and ignored `MPToken` and `MPTokenIssuance` entirely, so an MPT payment or clawback came back reporting only the XRP fee — a caller reconciling an MPT transfer got a confidently wrong "nothing moved" answer rather than an error.

## What changed

- `Balance` (`models/common/index.ts`) gains an optional `mpt_issuance_id`, and a doc comment spelling out the three row shapes. Use `mpt_issuance_id`, not `currency`, to recognise an MPT row: `'MPT'` is also a legal three-letter issued-currency code, but an issued-currency row never carries `mpt_issuance_id`. Adding an optional field leaves every existing XRP/issued-currency row untouched, so this is **not** a breaking change.
- `sugar/balances.ts` gains `formatMPTokenBalances`, which turns the `MPToken` entries of an `account_objects` page into `Balance` rows (`currency: 'MPT'`, `value` defaulting to `'0'` because rippled omits `MPTAmount` when the balance is zero) and optionally filters them by issuer, decoding the issuer's AccountID out of the 192-bit `MPTokenIssuanceID`.
- `Client.getBalances` issues a third paged request (`account_objects`, `type: 'mptoken'`) alongside the two it already made, appends those rows, and now declares `Promise<Balance[]>`. `peer` filters MPT rows by issuance issuer, mirroring what it already does to trust lines; `limit` still truncates the combined list.
- `utils/getBalanceChanges.ts` handles two more node types. An `MPToken` node yields the holder's `MPTAmount` delta; an `MPTokenIssuance` node yields the issuer's *negated* `OutstandingAmount` delta (issuing 100 units is `-100` for the issuer, clawing back 5 is `+5`), rebuilding the `mpt_issuance_id` from the node's `Issuer` and `Sequence` since rippled does not put the id on the metadata node. Amount fields absent from metadata are read as zero, and an empty `PreviousFields: {}` — how rippled signals an absent-to-present transition — is distinguished from a node where some *other* field (e.g. `Flags`) changed and the amount did not.

## How it was tested

All commands from a clean `npm ci` at the repo root.

- `npm run build` — success (7 projects).
- `npm test` in `packages/xrpl` — `135 suites / 1361 tests` passed, including 9 new `getBalanceChanges` MPT cases and 3 new `getBalances` cases. `getBalanceChanges.ts` statement coverage 98.87%.
- `npm run lint` at the root — clean for all 7 projects (`--max-warnings 0`).
- `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json` — exit 0.
- Integration: `PORT=6121 npm run test:integration -- -t "reports an MPT holding and the balance changes that created it"` against a throwaway `rippleci/xrpld:develop` standalone node — 1 passed. It creates a real issuance, authorizes a holder, pays 100 units, then asserts `getBalances` shows the MPT row (and that `peer` keeps/drops it correctly) and that `getBalanceChanges` on the payment's metadata shows `+100` for the holder and `-100` for the issuer.

The unit fixtures are real metadata captured from that standalone node, covering issuance create, authorize (create and delete), issuer→holder / holder→holder / holder→issuer payments, partial and full clawback, and an `MPTokenIssuanceSet` lock (the regression guard for "a non-amount field changed, so the amount did not").

Red-before check: with the source changes reverted, the new unit tests fail (the MPT rows and MPT balance changes are simply absent), and the four pre-existing `getBalances` tests fail against the new source until the mock rippled learns to answer `account_objects` — which is what proves the third request is really being made.

## Follow-ups (out of scope here)

- `getBalances`' `limit` is applied twice with different meanings: it is passed to each underlying request *and* used to slice the merged array, so `limit: 10` against an account with 10 trust lines hides every MPT. Pre-existing behaviour for XRP+trust lines; worth redefining, but a behaviour change of its own.
- The `Balance.value` of an MPT row is raw fractional units; there is no helper that applies the issuance's `AssetScale`, so callers must fetch the `MPTokenIssuance` themselves to display a human amount.
- `getBalanceChanges` still ignores other value-bearing ledger entries (e.g. `Escrow`, `PayChannel`), consistent with its pre-existing scope.

Finding ids: 053, 077.
title: fix(xrpl): report MPT holdings from getBalances and getBalanceChanges

Stacked on https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/40 (`fm/xrpljs-autofill-tickets-and-batch-sequences-f15`) — this PR targets that branch, so review it after #40 merges, or read only the last commit.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/20
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2
Audit finding **088**.

## The problem

`submitAndWait` resolves with `meta.TransactionResult === 'tesSUCCESS'` for a `Batch` whenever the *outer* transaction was processed — including when every inner transaction was reverted or skipped. A caller who checks the result code the way they would for any other transaction concludes the batch did what they asked, and nothing in the library says otherwise:

- the `Batch` model, `BatchFlags` and `BatchSigner` carried no doc comments at all, so the per-flag revert/skip semantics were undocumented;
- `ParentBatchID` on transaction metadata was an undocumented `string?`;
- an applied inner transaction lands in the ledger as its own validated transaction under its own hash, and there was no way to compute that hash, so the inner results were unreachable.

## What this changes

- **`getBatchInnerHashes(batch)`** (`src/utils/getBatchInnerHashes.ts`, exported from `utils`) — hashes each entry of `RawTransactions` in order. Inner transactions are unsigned and carry `tfInnerBatchTxn`, so `hashSignedTx` already computes the right hash for them; the helper just makes that reachable. Takes the `Batch` in the form it was submitted (post-`autofill`), since any differing field changes the hash.
- **`Client.getBatchResults(batch)`** (`src/sugar/getBatchResults.ts`) — takes a submitted `Batch` or an outer transaction hash and returns, per inner transaction in `RawTransactions` order: its `hash`, its `result` (`TransactionResult`, or the exported `BATCH_INNER_NOT_APPLIED` = `'not-applied'`), and the inner `tx` response when there is one. "Not applied" is detected by the inner `tx` lookup returning `txnNotFound` — the only signal rippled gives, since reverted and skipped inner transactions are not recorded at all. Passing a hash that is not a `Batch`, or an inner transaction that is not yet validated, throws `ValidationError`; any other `tx` error propagates.
- **Docs** — the `Batch` interface gains a description, an **Outcome model** `@remarks` section (what each of `tfAllOrNothing` / `tfOnlyOne` / `tfUntilFailure` / `tfIndependent` reverts or skips, how applied inners appear with `ParentBatchID`, and that there is no dry run because `simulate` does not support `Batch`) and an example; every `BatchFlags` member, `BatchSigner` and its fields, and `RawTransactions`/`BatchSigners` are documented. `ParentBatchID` in `metadata.ts` is documented. `Client.submit` and `Client.submitAndWait` now say what their result code does and does not tell you about a `Batch`.

`BatchInnerResult` and `BATCH_INNER_NOT_APPLIED` are exported from the package root.

## Tests

New unit tests: `test/utils/getBatchInnerHashes.test.ts` (3) and `test/client/getBatchResults.test.ts` (7, against mock rippled — mixed `tesSUCCESS` / `tec` / not-applied, a whole-batch revert, accepting the `Batch` object without refetching the outer, and each error path).

New integration test `test/integration/transactions/batchOutcomes.test.ts` reproduces the finding end to end: a `tfAllOrNothing` `Batch` whose second inner payment carries an unreachable `Sequence` resolves `submitAndWait` with outer `tesSUCCESS`, while `getBatchResults` reports **both** inner transactions as `not-applied`. A second case checks that applied inner transactions come back with their own `tesSUCCESS` and a `ParentBatchID` equal to the outer hash.

```
$ npm test                       # packages/xrpl  → 136 suites, 1361 tests passed
$ npx eslint . --max-warnings 0  # packages/xrpl  → clean
$ npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json              → clean
$ npm run lint                   # repo root      → clean, 7 projects
$ PORT=6118 npm run test:integration -- -t "Batch outcomes"   → 2 passed
```

Integration run was against a dedicated standalone `rippleci/xrpld:develop` node on port 6118, removed afterwards. This fork has no CI beyond Socket Security, so local runs are the gate.

## Follow-ups (not fixed here)

- `Client.getBatchResults` issues one `tx` request per inner transaction; a batch with many inners would benefit from `account_tx` filtered by `ParentBatchID` once rippled exposes that, but no such filter exists today.
- `simulate` rejects `Batch`, so there is still no way to preview inner outcomes before submitting. Worth raising upstream on rippled rather than patching here.
title: feat(xrpl): report per-inner Batch outcomes and document the Batch model (audit 088)

body:
Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/9
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Audit findings **017** (`Amount` excludes `MPTAmount`) and **057** (`Payment.Amount` is required but API v2 never returns it).

## What was wrong

**017 — the exported `Amount` type excluded MPT.** `models/common/index.ts` carried `// TODO: remove this once MPTv2 is released` above an `Amount` that was only `IssuedCurrencyAmount | string`, and the MPT case was bolted on at each use site as `Amount | MPTAmount`. MPT has been live since rippled 2.3, so the gate was never real. Meanwhile the runtime guard `isAmount` already accepted MPT values, so the library produced amounts its own public types rejected: anything typed on `Amount` (`NFTOffer.amount`, `PaymentMetadata.delivered_amount`, every helper taking an amount) refused a value the client had just handed back.

**057 — `Payment.Amount` was required, but no API v2 read path returns it.** rippled's API v2 — `DEFAULT_API_VERSION` for this client — renames a Payment's `Amount` to `DeliverMax` on every read: `tx`, `account_tx`, `transaction_entry`, transaction streams, and therefore `submitAndWait`. The types still claimed `Amount` was there and `DeliverMax` optional, so the compiler blessed `response.result.tx_json.Amount`, which is `undefined` at runtime, and offered no hint that `DeliverMax` is where the value lives.

## What changed

* `Amount` is now `IssuedCurrencyAmount | MPTAmount | string`. The hand-written `Amount | MPTAmount` unions (and their paired stale TODOs) collapse to `Amount` in `payment.ts`, `escrowCreate.ts`, `vaultDeposit.ts`, `vaultWithdraw.ts`, `loanPay.ts`, `loanBrokerCoverDeposit.ts`, `loanBrokerCoverWithdraw.ts` and `metadata.ts`. `ClawbackAmount` and `loanBrokerCoverClawback` keep their narrower `IssuedCurrencyAmount | MPTAmount` — XRP is genuinely not clawable.
* `Payment` splits into a shared `BasePayment` plus two shapes: `Payment` (submit shape, `Amount` required, `DeliverMax` optional alias) and the new `PaymentV2` (read shape, `DeliverMax` required, `Amount?: never`). `Payment` is unchanged for callers of `autofill`/`submit`.
* New `TransactionV2<T>` maps a transaction type to its API v2 read shape — one definition shared by `tx`, `account_tx`, `transaction_entry` and `subscribe`, so the v2 `tx_json` of each now says `DeliverMax`. The API v1 fields (`tx`, `transaction`) keep plain `Transaction`, which is correct: v1 really does return `Amount`.
* `isPartialPayment` accepts either shape, and its `amount === undefined` guard is now reachable rather than dead.

`PaymentV2` and `TransactionV2` are exported from the package root.

## BREAKING

Both changes are type-level; runtime behaviour is unchanged.

1. **`Amount` now includes `MPTAmount`.** Narrowing code that assumed two cases must handle three.

   ```ts
   // before
   const currency = typeof amount === 'string' ? 'XRP' : amount.currency
   // after
   const currency =
     typeof amount === 'string'
       ? 'XRP'
       : 'mpt_issuance_id' in amount
         ? amount.mpt_issuance_id
         : amount.currency
   ```

2. **API v2 reads expose `DeliverMax`, not `Amount`.**

   ```ts
   const tx = await client.submitAndWait(signed.tx_blob)
   // before: compiled, undefined at runtime
   const sent = tx.result.tx_json.Amount
   // after
   const sent = tx.result.tx_json.TransactionType === 'Payment'
     ? tx.result.tx_json.DeliverMax
     : undefined
   ```

   Passing such a `tx_json` to a helper typed on `Transaction` (for example `hashSignedTx`) now needs the value moved back:

   ```ts
   const forHashing = { ...tx_json, Amount: tx_json.DeliverMax }
   delete forHashing.DeliverMax
   ```

   Callers who want the old shape can keep requesting `api_version: 1`, whose types are untouched.

A `### BREAKING CHANGES` entry covering both is in `packages/xrpl/HISTORY.md` under Unreleased.

## Tests

Two new unit suites, red before this change and green after:

> **Stacked on https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/31** (`fm/xrpljs-codec-mpt-amount-hardening-f08`) — this PR targets that branch, not `main`. Review/merge #31 first; only the last commit here is new.

## What was wrong

The client-side MPT validators let through transactions that rippled rejects, so the failure surfaced as a `tem*`/`tec*` from the ledger instead of a local `ValidationError`. `validateMPTokenAuthorize` enforced nothing beyond `validateBaseTransaction` — `Holder === Account` and arbitrary flag bits both passed (014). `MPTokenIssuanceID` and `mpt_issuance_id` were validated as "any string", so a truncated or non-hex ID was only caught by the codec at signing time (036). `MPTAmount.value` was never validated at all, so `'0'`, `'-1'`, `'1.5'` and `'1e2'` all reached `Payment` and `Clawback` unexamined (016). `AssetScale` was validated only as "a number", accepting `300`, `-1` and `2.5` for a `UInt8` field (039). No MPT validator — nor `Clawback` — rejected flag bits outside the transaction's own mask, even though rippled answers those with `temINVALID_FLAG` (037). `isMPTIssuer` existed but no core MPT validator used it, despite the issuer's `AccountID` being the last 20 bytes of every `MPTokenIssuanceID` and therefore checkable offline (073). `isMPTAmount` and `isIssuedCurrencyAmount` counted raw `Object.keys`, so an object with an extra `undefined`-valued key — exactly what spreading an optional field produces, and what `JSON.stringify` drops — was rejected as malformed (075). And `validateMPTokenMetadata` parsed `uris[].category` as a free string, ignoring the XLS-89 enum (076).

## What changed

**`packages/xrpl/src/models/transactions/common.ts`** — the shared pieces:

- `isUInt8` / `isUInt16` / `isUInt32` integer-range guards.
- `isMPTokenIssuanceID` — exactly 48 hex characters (4-byte sequence + 20-byte issuer `AccountID`).
- `isMPTValue` — a canonical unsigned decimal integer string no greater than 2^63 − 1 (no sign, no exponent, no leading zeros, no whitespace).
- `tfUniversal` (`tfFullyCanonicalSig | tfInnerBatchTxn`) and `validateFlagsMask(tx, mask)`, which throws `"<TransactionType>: invalid Flags"` for a non-`UInt32` `Flags` or any bit inside the mask. Object-form `Flags` are left to `convertTxFlagsToNumber`.
- `isMPTAmount` / `isIssuedCurrencyAmount` now count only keys whose value is defined, and `isMPTAmount` delegates to the two new guards.

**Per-transaction**, each validator now exports a `tf*Mask` mirroring rippled's and enforces it:

| Transaction | Mask | Other checks added |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `MPTokenAuthorize` | `~(tfUniversal \| tfMPTUnauthorize)` | `MPTokenIssuanceID` shape; `Holder !== Account`; the issuer must name a `Holder`, a non-issuer must not |
| `MPTokenIssuanceDestroy` | `~tfUniversal` (defines no flags) | `MPTokenIssuanceID` shape; `Account` must be the issuer |
| `MPTokenIssuanceSet` | `~(tfUniversal \| tfMPTLock \| tfMPTUnlock \| enable-flag mask)` | `MPTokenIssuanceID` shape; `Account` must be the issuer; `TransferFee` must be an integer |
| `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` | `~(tfUniversal \| tfMPTCanLock \| tfMPTRequireAuth \| tfMPTCanEscrow \| tfMPTCanTrade \| tfMPTCanTransfer \| tfMPTCanClawback \| tfMPTCanHoldConfidentialBalance)` | `AssetScale` must be a `UInt8`; `TransferFee` must be an integer |
| `Clawback` | `~tfUniversal` (defines no flags) | an MPT `Amount` must have a non-zero canonical value and an `mpt_issuance_id` the `Account` issues |
| `Payment` | — | an MPT `Amount` must have a non-zero value |

The `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` mask deliberately excludes `0x1`: that bit is `lsfMPTLocked`, a ledger flag, not a valid create flag.

**`CredentialCreate`** — `Expiration` is a `UInt32` field and is now validated as one (the same "validated only as a number" bug as 039, in the file the finding's guard touches).

**`packages/xrpl/src/models/utils/mptokenMetadata.ts`** — `uris[].category` must be one of `website`, `social`, `docs`, `other`; a failed string check now `continue`s instead of falling through. The exact-three-keys rule on each `uris` entry is dropped, matching the tolerance the top level already grants.

**`packages/ripple-binary-codec/src/types/amount.ts`** — `isAmountObjectIOU` / `isAmountObjectMPT` ignore `undefined`-valued keys, so an amount object serialises as the shape it JSON-stringifies to (the codec half of 075).

A changelog line is added under the topmost unreleased section of both `packages/xrpl/HISTORY.md` and `packages/ripple-binary-codec/HISTORY.md`. No breaking change: every newly rejected input was already rejected by rippled.

## Findings covered

`014`, `016`, `036`, `037`, `039`, `073`, `075`, `076`.

## How this was tested

Tests were written first and confirmed red against the unmodified validators (28 new assertions failing), then green after the fix.

New / extended specs: `test/models/mptGuards.test.ts` (new — the guards and `validateFlagsMask` directly), `MPTokenAuthorize.test.ts` (rewritten), `MPTokenIssuanceDestroy.test.ts` (rewritten), `MPTokenIssuanceSet.test.ts`, `MPTokenIssuanceCreate.test.ts`, `clawback.test.ts`, `payment.test.ts`, `CredentialCreate.test.ts`, the `mptokenMetadataValidationData.json` fixture, and `packages/ripple-binary-codec/test/amount.test.ts`. The MPT fixtures now use an issuer-consistent ID (`000004C40596915CFDEEE3A695B3EFD6BDA9AC788A368B7B` embeds the shared fixture issuer's `AccountID`) plus a deliberately foreign one for the negative cases.

```
$ cd packages/xrpl && npm test
Test Suites: 135 passed, 135 total
Tests:       1380 passed, 1380 total

$ cd packages/ripple-binary-codec && npm test
Test Suites: 19 passed, 19 total
Tests:       1298 passed, 1298 total

$ npm run lint            # repo root
Successfully ran target lint for 7 projects

$ npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json                 # exit 0
$ npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/ripple-binary-codec/tsconfig.json  # exit 0
```

No integration test: this is pure client-side validation, with no change to autofill, signing or submission behaviour against a ledger. Note that this fork runs no GitHub Actions CI (only Socket Security checks), so the local results above are the gate.

## Follow-ups (not fixed here)

- **`VaultClawback` issuer check (part of 073).** The finding names `vaultClawback.ts`, but its issuer check is against the vault's asset issuer read from the ledger (`vaultAsset.getIssuer()`), which is not derivable from the transaction alone the way an `MPTokenIssuanceID`'s issuer is. Deferred rather than half-implemented.
- **`AssetScale`-aware conversion helpers (the second half of 016).** `mptToUnits` / `unitsToMpt` — the analogue of `xrpToDrops` / `dropsToXrp` for MPTs — belong with the other MPT helpers, not in the validators; they are scoped to the `mpt-helpers` unit.
- The `Expiration`-style "validated only as a number" pattern almost certainly recurs on other `UInt32` fields outside the MPT surface; `isUInt32` is now exported and ready for a sweep.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/12
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

body:
Audit finding **004**.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/7
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

## What was wrong

```ts
export interface BaseTransaction extends Record<string, unknown> {
```

Every transaction interface extends `BaseTransaction`, so every one of them inherited an index signature. An index signature makes `keyof T` widen to `string | number`, and that quietly breaks the type-level tools built on top of it:

- `Omit<Payment, 'Destination'>` and `Pick<...>` no-op — the omitted key is still assignable, because the index signature puts it back.
- `Partial<T>`, `Required<T>` and mapped types over `keyof T` lose the field union.
- Excess property checking never fires, so `{ ...payment, Destinaton: addr }` (typo) compiles, and so does any junk key.
- Reading `tx.AnythingAtAll` off a typed transaction type-checks and yields `unknown` rather than erroring.

The result is that the model layer provided approximately no protection on field names — the exact class of bug the models exist to catch, and one that matters for an MPT issuance flow where `MPTokenIssuanceID`, `Holder` and the lock flags all have near-miss spellings.

## What changed

**`src/models/transactions/common.ts`** — one line:

```diff
-export interface BaseTransaction extends Record<string, unknown> {
+export interface BaseTransaction {
```

**`src/models/transactions/transaction.ts`** — the escape hatch for the boundaries that genuinely need it, plus a widened `validate` signature:

```ts
/**
 * A transaction that may carry fields the models do not (yet) declare.
 * Use this type at forward-compatible boundaries instead: decoded blobs,
 * ledger responses, or literals that must carry a field newer than this library.
 */
export type LenientTransaction = Transaction & Record<string, unknown>
```

```diff
-export function validate(transaction: Record<string, unknown>): void {
+export function validate(
+  transaction: BaseTransaction | Record<string, unknown>,
+): void {
```

`LenientTransaction` is re-exported from `src/models/transactions/index.ts`, so it reaches the package root.

**Call sites that had leaned on the index signature** (the full blast radius — the build found exactly four source errors):

- `src/sugar/autofill.ts` — `fetchCounterPartySignersCount` is now typed `LoanSet` rather than `Transaction`; `Counterparty` and `LoanBrokerID` only exist there, and it is only ever called for a `LoanSet`. `convertToClassicAddress` does its dynamic field lookup through one explicit `Record<string, unknown>` local instead of relying on the transaction type being indexable.
- `src/Wallet/batchSigner.ts` — `signMultiBatch` narrows with `'Counterparty' in raw.RawTransaction` instead of casting the inner transaction to a record. This also drops an eslint-disable.
- `src/Wallet/{batchSigner,counterpartySigner,index,signer,sponsorSigner}.ts` — seven occurrences of

  ```ts
  // eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/consistent-type-assertions -- validate does not accept Transaction type
  validate(tx as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)
  ```

  are now just `validate(tx)`. The comment's premise is no longer true.

Runtime behaviour is unchanged throughout: this is a types-only fix plus the mechanical call-site updates it forces.

## Tests

New `test/models/transactionTypes.test.ts` asserts the property at the type level with `@ts-expect-error`, which fails the suite at compile time (ts-jest type-checks before running) if the index signature ever comes back:

1. `keyof MPTokenIssuanceSet` is the literal field union, not `string`.
2. Unknown field names are rejected in both a full literal and a `Partial<Payment>`.
3. `Omit` actually removes the key, and the remaining required fields stay required.
4. `LenientTransaction` still accepts a field from a future amendment.
5. `validate()` takes a typed transaction with no cast.

Two existing suites needed narrowing now that `Transaction` no longer exposes unmodelled fields: `test/wallet/sponsorSigner.test.ts` casts the three `Transaction` results to `Payment` before reading `Destination`/`Amount`, and `test/models/vaultWithdraw.test.ts` drops one redundant direct validator call that `assertValid` on the next line already covers.

**Red/green proof.** With this branch's `common.ts` swapped back for the one on `main` (and `jest --no-cache`, since ts-jest caches compilation and otherwise reports a false green), the new suite fails to compile with 6 errors and runs 0 tests:

```
TS2322 at line 34, and TS2578 "Unused '@ts-expect-error' directive" at 41, 53, 57, 70, 73
```

With the fix in place, `--no-cache` gives 5 passed.

## Checks run

This fork has no GitHub Actions configured (only Socket Security reports on PRs), so local runs are the gate. All from the repo root, all green:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `npm run build` | exit 0 |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0 (`--max-warnings 0`) |
| `npm test` in `packages/xrpl` | 135 suites, 1344 tests, exit 0 |
| `npx tsc --noEmit --target es2020 -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.eslint.json` | clean, except 7 pre-existing `Cannot find module 'xrpl'` errors in AMM integration tests that resolve from `dist/npm` |

No integration test: this unit changes no runtime ledger behaviour, so no `rippled` container was started.

## BREAKING

Transaction interfaces are now strict. Two patterns stop compiling:

**Assigning extra keys to a typed transaction.**

```ts
const tx: Payment = { ...base, SomeNewField: 1 }  // now an error
```

Migrate to the new type, an explicit intersection, or a cast:

```ts
const tx: LenientTransaction = { ...base, SomeNewField: 1 }
const tx: Payment & Record<string, unknown> = { ...base, SomeNewField: 1 }
```

**Reading an unmodelled field off a `Transaction`.** Functions typed to return `Transaction` (for example `signAsSponsor`, `combineSponsorSigners`, `addPreFundedSponsor`) no longer let you reach through to a subtype's fields. Narrow first:

```ts
const payment = signAsSponsor(wallet, tx).tx as Payment
payment.Destination
```

`validate()` now accepts `BaseTransaction | Record<string, unknown>`, so the inverse migration also applies: `validate(tx as unknown as Record<string, unknown>)` can be simplified to `validate(tx)`.

This is a compile-time break only. No runtime behaviour changes, and JavaScript consumers are unaffected.

## Follow-ups (not fixed here — adjacent, out of scope for this unit)

- The individual `validate*` functions (`validatePayment`, `validateBatch`, `validateVaultWithdraw`, …) still take `Record<string, unknown>` and so still require a cast at typed call sites. They could take `BaseTransaction | Record<string, unknown>` the way `validate` now does; that is a wider change across every model file.
- `test/models/*` helpers like `assertValid` are typed `any`, which hides exactly this class of regression in the model test suite.
- `convertToClassicAddress` looks up fields by string name at runtime. With `keyof` now meaningful, it could be typed against the actual field unions instead of going through a record.
title: fix(xrpl)!: make transaction types strict by dropping the BaseTransaction index signature

body:
## What was wrong

`submitAndWait` misreported outcomes in several ways. Its poll loop compared the validated ledger index against `LastLedgerSequence` *before* looking the transaction up, so when two or more ledgers closed between polls a transaction validated in its last allowed ledger was thrown as "expired" with `Preliminary result: tesSUCCESS` (062). Any `tx` lookup failure other than `txnNotFound` was re-thrown as a plain `Error` whose message started with the literal `undefined`, losing the original class and `data` (063). Failure surfaced through three unrelated shapes: `tem*` threw a string-built `XrplError`, `tec*` resolved, and `tef*`/`tel*` polled until expiry, so a `tefPAST_SEQ` from a concurrent submission showed up ~9 s later looking like a network expiry (025, 081). The `@throws` doc claimed that a transaction which "cannot be included in a validated ledger", including "insufficient balance", rejects, while every `tec*` outcome resolves normally (043).

## What changed

- **`TransactionFailedError`** (new, extends `XrplError`) with typed `engineResult`, `engineResultMessage` and `phase: 'submit' | 'expired'`; `data` carries the `submit` result when there is one. Exported from the package root.
- **Poll order** (`waitForFinalTransactionOutcome`): read the validated ledger index, then look the transaction up, return it if validated, and only then compare against `LastLedgerSequence`. Reading the index *before* the lookup makes the check race-free: if the index is already past `LastLedgerSequence`, every ledger the transaction could be in is validated, so a non-validated lookup is final. The audit proposed lookup-then-index, which leaves a window where the transaction validates between the two calls; this order closes it.
- **Lookup errors**: `txnNotFound` keeps polling; any other `XrplError` (`TimeoutError`, `DisconnectedError`, `RippledError` such as `tooBusy`) propagates unchanged; a non-library error is wrapped in an `XrplError` whose `data` is the cause. No more `undefined` prefix.
- **Terminal preliminary results**: `tem*`, `tef*` and `tel*` throw `TransactionFailedError` with `phase: 'submit'` immediately. The audit proposed throwing outright; live probing showed that rippled *keeps* a rejected `tefPAST_SEQ` transaction in its local cache and `tx` returns it with `validated: false`, so "rippled knows the hash" is not a usable signal. The rule is therefore: `tef*`/`tel*` do a single `tx` lookup and resolve only if it is already **validated** (re-submitting a signed blob after a disconnect, the pattern xrpl.org's reliable-submission guide recommends), otherwise throw. `tefALREADY` is excluded from the terminal set because rippled is saying the exact transaction is in the open ledger, so polling continues. The `tem*` message text is unchanged (`Transaction failed, temMALFORMED: ...`); the expiry message text is unchanged too, but its class is now `TransactionFailedError` with `phase: 'expired'` and `engineResult` set to the preliminary result.
- **Docs**: the `@throws` block on `submitAndWait` now lists exactly what throws (`ValidationError`, `TransactionFailedError` by phase, `ConnectionError`, `RippledError`), states up front that validated `tec*` results resolve with the fee charged and must be read from `meta.TransactionResult`, and carries a `@remarks` on the one-in-flight-per-account constraint and Tickets.
- **Helpers**: `getTransactionResultCode` and `isTesSuccess` cherry-picked (authorship preserved) from `origin/add-transaction-result-helpers`.
- **Integration harness**: `test/integration/submitAndWait.test.ts` no longer scrapes `Preliminary result:` out of the message; it reads `err.engineResult` from the typed error.
- `HISTORY.md`: entries under Unreleased / Added and Fixed.

Finding 081's optional per-account sequence reservation is **not** implemented: it adds client state and a new failure mode, and the finding offers the doc note plus immediate `tef*` reporting as the non-breaking alternative. Left as a possible follow-up.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/16
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

## How it was tested

```
npm ci && npm run build                                   # ok
cd packages/xrpl && npm test                              # 136 suites, 1362 tests passed
npm run lint  (root)                                      # 0 errors, 0 warnings, all 7 packages
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json           # ok
docker run --detach --publish 6114:6006 --volume "$PWD/.ci-config/:/etc/xrpld/" \
  --name xrpld-submitandwait-outcomes rippleci/xrpld:develop --standalone
PORT=6114 npm run test:integration -- test/integration/submitAndWait.test.ts   # 8 passed
```

Red before / green after, verified by running the new tests against the pre-fix `sugar/submit.ts` and `client/index.ts`:

- Unit (`test/client/submitAndWait.test.ts`, mock rippled): 8 of the 11 new tests fail on the old code (tem/tef/tel typing and immediacy, 062 last-ledger validation, expiry typing, tooBusy `RippledError` propagation, `TimeoutError` propagation, non-library error wrapping). The other 3 pin behaviour that must not change (re-submission of a validated blob resolves, polling continues while not found, `tec*` resolves).
- Integration (standalone rippled): "returns a transaction validated in its last allowed ledger even when the validated ledger has moved past it" (062's live repro: `LastLedgerSequence = validated + 1`, two `ledger_accept`s before the first poll) fails on the old code and passes now; "throws TransactionFailedError immediately for tefPAST_SEQ" hits the 60 s jest timeout on the old code (no ledger closes, so expiry never comes) and returns in under a second now. Also added: re-submitting a validated blob resolves with the same hash; a `tecUNFUNDED_PAYMENT` payment resolves and `isTesSuccess(getTransactionResultCode(meta))` is false.
- `test/client/errors.test.ts`: `TransactionFailedError` shape and `toString()`.

The fork has no GitHub Actions runs configured (only Socket Security checks), so the local checks above are the gate.

## Follow-ups discovered (not fixed here)

- On mainnet there is a window where an earlier submission of the same blob sits in a closed-but-not-yet-validated ledger; a re-submission then gets `tefPAST_SEQ` with a not-yet-validated lookup and is now thrown rather than polled. The typed error carries `engineResult: 'tefPAST_SEQ'` and the docs say to look the hash up before re-submitting, which is xrpl.org's guidance anyway. Standalone cannot reproduce this state. If it matters, `handleTerminalSubmission` could poll one extra `LEDGER_CLOSE_TIME` before throwing.
- `LEDGER_CLOSE_TIME` (1 s poll) is a hard-coded constant in `sugar/submit.ts`; making it a `submitAndWait` option would let fast standalone nodes and slow test networks tune it. Out of scope.
- `XrplError.data` is still `unknown` (finding 035, separate unit); `isTxnNotFound` in `sugar/submit.ts` narrows it locally and can be simplified once `RippledError.data` is typed.
