Stacked on https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/34 (`fm/xrpljs-mpt-transaction-docs-f25`); GitHub will retarget this PR to `main` once that one merges. The diff shown here is only this unit's commit.

## What was wrong

The captain's requirement "pre-emptively ban an address, and freeze it when it is banned" has no single on-ledger representation for MPTs: XLS-33 has no deny-list, nothing can be written on-ledger about an address before it opts in (`MPTokenAuthorize` / `MPTokenIssuanceSet` with `Holder` fail with `tecOBJECT_NOT_FOUND`), and opt-in cannot be prevented. The SDK's types described the fields but none of the three partial mechanisms (allow-listing under `lsfMPTRequireAuth`, lock-on-arrival, permissioned-domain admission) or their limits, and `tfMPTRequireAuth`'s comment ("limit who can hold their assets") reads as if it were a deny-list. An integrator had to discover all of this against a live node.

## What changed

Docs only; no runtime or type change.

- `MPTokenAuthorize`: new "Compliance controls: banning and freezing holders" section with a goal/mechanism table and the limits of each route (allow-listing is implicit and needs an off-ledger registry; opt-in cannot be prevented and the inert entry still costs the holder its reserve; a per-holder lock needs the MPToken to exist, works on a zero-balance unauthorized entry, survives a later authorization because `tecLOCKED` beats `tecNO_AUTH`, and pins the holder's reserve; credential revocation blocks payments but neither locks nor claws back and cannot combine `DomainID` with `Holder`; rippled cannot enumerate holders so lock-on-arrival means polling `ledger_entry`; ban a current holder with lock + `Clawback`).
- `MPTokenAuthorize.Holder`, `MPTokenIssuanceSet.Holder`: `@remarks` that the holder's MPToken must already exist (`tecOBJECT_NOT_FOUND` otherwise), so nothing can be pre-approved or pre-banned, with a pointer to the section.
- `MPTokenIssuanceSet.DomainID` and `MPTokenIssuanceCreateFlags.tfMPTRequireAuth`: one-paragraph cross-references (allow-list not deny-list; what credential revocation does and does not do).
- `packages/xrpl/HISTORY.md`: changelog line under Unreleased / Fixed.

The section lives in the transaction doc comments rather than a README because `packages/xrpl/README.md` (listed in the plan) does not exist; the root `README.md` is a quickstart and typedoc landing page with no feature-level sections, while the doc comments render on js.xrpl.org and in IDE hovers where the fields are used. The audit's proposed table was kept to two columns because this repo lints doc comments at 130 columns with zero warnings allowed; the limits moved to a bullet list.

npx jest --config jest.config.unit.js test/models/MPTokenAuthorize.test.ts \

                                                          # 3 suites, 48 tests passed

## What was wrong

Several RPC request/response models in `packages/xrpl/src/models` were written from a single example and disagree with what rippled actually parses or emits. `LedgerEntryRequest.credential` was typed with `credentialType`, the one spelling rippled rejects (`Missing field 'credential_type'`), and the request had no typed lookups for `permissioned_domain`, `vault`, `oracle`, `nft_offer`, `loan` or `loan_broker`. The `ledger_entry` result required `ledger_current_index`, which is absent on every closed/validated lookup, and omitted the `ledger_index`/`ledger_hash` those lookups return. `feature` entries were typed as `{ enabled, name, supported }` with no `vetoed` or vote counts. The `Escrow` ledger type declared `Amount: string` and `IssuerNode?: number` although a token escrow's `Amount` is an object and `IssuerNode` is a UInt64 hex string like `OwnerNode`. `LedgerDataLabeledLedgerEntry` required a lowercase `ledgerEntryType` field that rippled never emits.

## What changed

- `models/methods/ledgerEntry.ts`
  - `credential.credential_type` (was `credentialType`).
  - New lookups, shaped after rippled's `LedgerEntry.cpp` parsers: `permissioned_domain: { account, seq } | string`, `vault: { owner, seq } | string`, `oracle: { account, oracle_document_id } | string`, `nft_offer: string`, `loan: { loan_broker_id, loan_seq } | string`, `loan_broker: { owner, seq } | string`.
  - `LedgerEntryResponseResultBase`: `ledger_current_index?`, plus `ledger_index?` and `ledger_hash?`, matching `AccountObjectsResponse`.
- `models/methods/feature.ts`: new exported `FeatureInfo` used by both `FeatureAllResponse` and `FeatureOneResponse`, adding `vetoed?: boolean | 'Obsolete'`, `count?`, `validations?`, `threshold?`, `majority?`.
- `models/ledger/Escrow.ts`: `Amount: Amount | MPTAmount`, `IssuerNode?: string`.
- `models/methods/ledgerData.ts`: `LedgerDataLabeledLedgerEntry = LedgerEntry`.
- `HISTORY.md`: changelog line under Unreleased / Fixed.

### Deviations from the audit's proposed fix

- **`vetoed` is optional, not required.** rippled's `AmendmentTable::injectJson` only emits `vetoed`, `count`, `validations` and `threshold` for admin connections and only for amendments that are not yet enabled. A public server, or an enabled amendment, has none of them. The audit saw them because a standalone node's websocket is admin.
- **No `vote` field.** Neither rippled's `Feature.cpp`/`AmendmentTable.cpp` nor xrpl.org emit or document a `vote` output field; adding it would be a phantom field of the same kind finding 060 removes.
- **`majority` is a time**, not a ledger index: rippled sets it from the `Amendments` ledger entry's `Majorities` as seconds since the Ripple Epoch. Documented that way on the type.
- `loan` uses `loan_seq` (rippled and xrpl.org), not `loan_sequence`.

The `BaseRequest` index-signature removal from finding 055 is intentionally not here; it belongs to the `strict-request-types` unit.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/6
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Findings covered: 018, 032, 054, 055 (lookup members only), 056, 060.

## Breaking?

No. Required fields were loosened, fields were added, `credentialType` never produced a working request, `ledgerEntryType` was never present at runtime, and `Escrow.Amount`/`IssuerNode` now match what rippled sends. Readers that assumed `Escrow.Amount` is always a string will see a type error, which is the bug surfacing.

## How it was tested

New unit tests, all compile-time-plus-runtime, each verified red against the original types (`git checkout -- src`, `jest --no-cache`: 3 suites fail with the expected `TS2339`/`TS2322` errors) and green after:

- `packages/xrpl/test/models/ledgerEntry.test.ts` - `credential_type` request; the six new lookups keep rippled's key names and expose sub-fields without casts; validated result exposes `ledger_index`/`ledger_hash`, current-ledger result exposes `ledger_current_index`; `Escrow` node accepts XRP, IOU and MPT amounts and a hex `IssuerNode`.
- `packages/xrpl/test/models/feature.test.ts` - `FeatureAllResponse`/`FeatureOneResponse` entries expose `vetoed` (`true` and `'Obsolete'`), `count`, `validations`, `threshold`, `majority`.
- `packages/xrpl/test/models/ledgerData.test.ts` - JSON state entries are plain ledger entries; `'data' in entry` discriminates binary vs JSON.

Integration tests added to `packages/xrpl/test/integration/requests/ledgerEntry.test.ts` and run against my own standalone `rippleci/xrpld:develop` (3.4.0-rc1) on port 6104:

- `validated lookup returns ledger_index and ledger_hash` - `account_root` with `ledger_index: 'validated'` returns `validated: true`, numeric `ledger_index`, string `ledger_hash`, no `ledger_current_index`.
- `credential lookup by subject, issuer and credential_type` - `CredentialCreate` + `CredentialAccept`, then `ledger_entry` with `credential: { subject, issuer, credential_type }` type-checks and returns the `Credential` entry (acceptance criterion from the sub-issue).

Commands and results (this fork has no GitHub Actions runs, so local checks are the gate):

```
npm ci && npm run build                                   # ok
cd packages/xrpl && npm test                              # 137 suites, 1348 tests passed
npm run lint                                              # (repo root) 0 errors, 0 warnings
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json           # ok
PORT=6104 npm run test:integration -- test/integration/requests/ledgerEntry.test.ts
                                                          # 6 passed (4 existing + 2 new)
```

## Follow-ups discovered (not fixed here)

- `FeatureInfo.name` is typed required but rippled only emits it when the name is non-empty (xrpl.org: "May be omitted"). Left as is to avoid breaking readers; worth a look in a later pass.
- `FeatureAllResponse` / `FeatureOneResponse` are not re-exported from the package index (only `FeatureRequest`/`FeatureResponse` and now `FeatureInfo` are); consumers who want the narrowed shapes must import from `models/methods/feature`.
title: fix(xrpl): correct ledger_entry, feature, ledger_data and Escrow RPC shapes

body:
## What was wrong

The validators for `Payment`, `EscrowCreate`/`EscrowFinish`, the credential and permissioned-domain transactions and `DelegateSet` were shape-only, and several of them predate MPTs: an MPT `Payment` with `Paths`, an XRP `SendMax` or a zero value passed `validate()` and failed on rippled with `temMALFORMED`/`temBAD_AMOUNT`; a self-payment passed and failed with `temREDUNDANT`; `handleDeliverMax` compared `Amount` and `DeliverMax` by reference so two equal MPT/IOU objects were rejected; `Account` was checked with `isString`, so a mis-pasted issuer address surfaced as the address codec's `checksum_invalid`/`Unknown letter` at sign time; `Holder`/`Subject`/`Issuer` were skipped by autofill's X-address normalization and the same-account checks compared raw strings; escrow, credential and domain validators missed the preflight rules a token escrow or a domain hits; and the MPT granular permissions `MPTokenIssuanceLock`/`MPTokenIssuanceUnlock` existed only inside the binary codec, with `PermissionValue` typed as `string` and any name accepted.

## What changed

- **Payment** (`payment.ts`): rejects `Account === Destination` (after X-address normalization) unless `Paths` or a `SendMax` in a different currency make it a conversion; rejects MPT payments with `Paths`, with a `SendMax`/`DeliverMin` in another asset, or with a zero value. `DeliverMax` is accepted as the API v2 alias of `Amount` (either one is required) and must equal `Amount` when both are present. Doc comments on `Amount`, `DeliverMax`, `Paths`, `SendMax`, `DeliverMin` mention the MPT rules.
- **autofill** (`sugar/autofill.ts`): `handleDeliverMax` uses `amountsEqual` (moved from `client/partialPayment.ts` to `models/transactions/common.ts`, exported together with a new `isSameAsset`); `setValidAddresses` also normalizes `Holder`, `Subject`, `Issuer` and `Delegate`.
- **common** (`common.ts`): `Account` is validated with `isAccount`; `isAuthorizeCredential` requires an address `Issuer` and a 1–64 byte even-length hex `CredentialType` (new `isCredentialType` guard, also applied to the top-level `CredentialType`); `CredentialIDs` entries must be 64-hex ledger entry ids; `containsDuplicates` compares decoded bytes (uppercased hex, classic address).
- **Escrow** (`escrowCreate.ts`, `escrowFinish.ts`): `CancelAfter` must be strictly after `FinishAfter`; `Amount` must be positive (XRP, IOU or MPT); `Condition` must be hex; on `EscrowFinish`, `Condition` and `Fulfillment` must be supplied together and be hex.
- **Domains/credentials** (`permissionedDomainSet.ts`, `permissionedDomainDelete.ts`, `CredentialCreate.ts`, `CredentialAccept.ts`, `CredentialDelete.ts`): `DomainID` uses `isDomainID` (zero hash rejected, matching rippled's `temMALFORMED`); `Subject`/`Issuer` use `isAccount` and are typed `Account`; the `AcceptedCredentials` doc no longer claims an empty array deletes the field.
- **Same-account checks** (`clawback.ts`, `AMMClawback.ts`, `MPTokenIssuanceSet.ts`, `delegateSet.ts`): use `areAddressesEqual`, so an X-address form no longer bypasses the check (and `AMMClawback` no longer over-rejects an X-address `Account` that matches `Asset.issuer`).
- **DelegateSet** (`delegateSet.ts`): new exported `GranularPermission` enum (all twelve codec names, including the two MPT ones) and `PermissionValue` type; `validate()` rejects a `PermissionValue` that is neither a transaction type nor a granular permission (the existing non-delegatable deny-list is kept).
- `HISTORY.md` entries under Unreleased.
- Test fixtures: `sponsorshipSet`/`sponsorshipTransfer`/`validateSponsorship` used an `Account` with an invalid checksum, exactly the input finding 066 describes; swapped for a valid address.

Deviation from the proposed fix for 042: the `Payment.Amount` type is left required. Making it optional widens the type for every reader of `payment.Amount` (including several places inside the library) and is a larger break than this unit warrants; the runtime now accepts `DeliverMax`-only, so the `as unknown as Payment` cast in the integration test is the only remaining friction. Left as a follow-up for the captain.

## BREAKING

`Permission.PermissionValue` is now typed `PermissionValue` (`Transaction['TransactionType'] | GranularPermission`) instead of `string`. Literal permission names and `GranularPermission` members compile unchanged. Code that assigns a plain `string` variable (for example a name read from config) needs a cast or a runtime check:

```ts
import { GranularPermission, TRANSACTION_TYPES } from 'xrpl'
const known = Object.values(GranularPermission).includes(name) || TRANSACTION_TYPES.includes(name)
```

Everything else is stricter validation of input rippled already rejects.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/13
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Findings covered: 040, 041, 042, 066, 068, 072, 074, 089.

## How it was tested

Unit tests added in `test/models/{payment,baseTransaction,escrowCreate,escrowFinish,permissionedDomainSet,permissionedDomainDelete,CredentialCreate,CredentialAccept,CredentialDelete,delegateSet,MPTokenIssuanceSet,clawback,AMMClawback,utils}.test.ts` and `test/client/autofill.test.ts`. Against the pre-fix source (tests kept, `src` checked out from `main`) they fail; against this branch they pass:

```
# pre-fix src, new tests:  Test Suites: 15 failed, 65 passed  Tests: 49 failed, 907 passed
# this branch (packages/xrpl) npm test:   Test Suites: 134 passed  Tests: 1400 passed
npm run lint (root)                       exit 0
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json   ok
npm run build                             ok
```

Integration (autofill behaviour changed), against my own standalone node `rippleci/xrpld:develop` on port 6111 (`PORT=6111 npm run test:integration -- <files>`): `clawback` (extended with a tagged X-address `Holder`, which autofill now normalizes and rippled accepts), `permissionedDomain`, `permissionedDEX`, `payment`, `escrowCreate`, `escrowFinish`, `escrowCancel`, `credentialCreate`, `credentialAccept`, `credentialDelete`, `delegateSet`, `mptokenIssuanceSet`, `ammClawback`:

```
Test Suites: 13 passed, 13 total   Tests: 30 passed, 30 total
```

The fork has no Actions workflows running on PRs, so local checks are the gate.

## Follow-ups noticed (not changed here)

- `ConfidentialMPTClawback` (`Account === Holder`), `ConfidentialMPTSend` (`Account === Destination`) and `NFTokenMint` (`Account === Issuer`) still compare addresses textually; same pattern as 068, outside this unit's file list.
- `Payment.Amount` optional / `Payment = PaymentWithAmount | PaymentWithDeliverMax` typing (042, see above).
- `isDomainID` rejects the zero hash everywhere; finding 038 covers the transactions where a zero `DomainID` is a valid "clear" value.
- The self-payment check mirrors rippled by comparing IOU currency codes only; `isSameAsset` (issuer-aware) is used for the MPT `SendMax`/`DeliverMin` rules.
title: fix(xrpl)!: tighten Payment, Escrow, Credential/Domain and DelegateSet validators (MPT rules, address checks, DeliverMax equality, GranularPermission)

body:
## What was wrong

`validateBatch` only checked the inner-transaction rules, so a Batch with no mode flag, two mode flags, 0/1/9 inner transactions, or a `Delegate` on the outer transaction passed `validate()` and every co-signer signed it before rippled returned `temINVALID_FLAG` / `temARRAY_EMPTY` / an RPC error; rippled's `simulate` cannot dry-run a Batch, so there was no other pre-submission check. The `Batch` type was looser than the validator in one direction (nested Batch, inner `Fee: '12'`, `TxnSignature`, `LastLedgerSequence` all compiled) and stricter than the rest of the SDK in the other (`Flags: { tfAllOrNothing: true }` did not compile). And `autofill`'s Batch fee had no term for `BatchSigners`, while its only knob, `signersCount`, was documented as "only used for multisigned transactions"; the repo's own integration test worked around it with `autofill(tx, 1)`. Verified live on a standalone `rippleci/xrpld:develop` node: a two-account Batch autofilled by the old code is rejected with `telINSUF_FEE_P`, and one more base fee makes it `tesSUCCESS`.

## What changed

- **`validateBatch`** (`packages/xrpl/src/models/transactions/batch.ts`): requires exactly one of `tfAllOrNothing | tfOnlyOne | tfUntilFailure | tfIndependent` (number or object-form `Flags`), 2–8 `RawTransactions`, and no `Delegate` on the outer Batch (the SDK already lists `Batch` as non-delegable in `delegateSet.ts`). Messages follow the existing `Batch: ...` style.
- **Types**: new exported `BatchInnerTransaction = Exclude<SubmittableTransaction, Batch> & { Fee?: '0'; SigningPubKey?: ''; TxnSignature?: never; Signers?: never; LastLedgerSequence?: never }`, used by `Batch.RawTransactions`; `Batch.Flags?: number | BatchFlagsInterface`. The confidential Batch assembler (`confidential/batch.ts`) narrows to the new type at its single `shapeInner` step.
- **Fee** (`packages/xrpl/src/sugar/autofill.ts`): the Batch branch adds `BaseFee × countBatchSignatures(tx)`, mirroring rippled's `Batch::calculateBaseFee`: when `BatchSigners` is present, one per `TxnSignature` plus each multisigned signer's `Signers.length`; otherwise one per account rippled requires as a batch signer (each inner's `Delegate ?? Account`, `Counterparty`, and `Sponsor` with a `SponsorSignature`, excluding the outer account). `signersCount` reverts to meaning the transaction's own multisign signers; the `Client.autofill`, `getTransactionFee`, and `ConfidentialBatchParams.signersCount` docs now say so.
- **`Client.simulate` doc**: notes rippled answers `Not implemented` for a Batch.
- **Tests**: fixed the invalid `Flags: 1` fixtures in `test/models/batch.test.ts` and `test/wallet/batchSigner.test.ts` (the signer test's expected signatures are regenerated; they are deterministic RFC 6979 / RFC 8032 signatures over the corrected flag); new validator cases; a `@ts-expect-error` type test; six fee cases; `test/integration/transactions/batch.test.ts` now autofills the two-account batch with no `signersCount`.
- `packages/xrpl/HISTORY.md` entries under Unreleased.

### Deviation from the proposed fix

The proposal also rejected a `BatchSigner` whose `Account` equals the outer account. That rule is dropped: `combineBatchSigners` deliberately accepts a submitter-signed transaction and strips that signer (test "removes signer for Batch submitter"), and it calls `validate()` on each input first, so the rule would break that documented flow. rippled still rejects it at submit with `temBAD_SIGNER`.

## BREAKING

`Batch.RawTransactions[].RawTransaction` is now `BatchInnerTransaction`. Inline inner objects, and objects that already satisfy the rules, are unaffected, but a variable declared with a transaction type whose fields are wider than the inner rules (for example `const payment: Payment = {...}`, where `Fee?: string`) is no longer assignable, even when it sets no `Fee`. The sub-issue expected this to be non-breaking; it is not for that common pattern (the repo's own integration test hit it). Migration:

```ts
// before
const payment: Payment = { TransactionType: 'Payment', Flags: 0x40000000, Account, Destination, Amount }
// after: declare the inner as a Batch inner ...
const payment: BatchInnerTransaction = { TransactionType: 'Payment', Flags: 0x40000000, Account, Destination, Amount }
// ... or keep the literal's inferred type
const payment = { TransactionType: 'Payment', Flags: 0x40000000, Account, Destination, Amount } satisfies Payment
```

If the fork prefers the non-breaking variant, reduce `BatchInnerTransaction` to `Exclude<SubmittableTransaction, Batch>` (still rejects nested Batches; drops the compile-time `Fee`/signature checks, which `validate` and `autofill` still enforce at runtime).

## Findings covered

099, 092, 091 (audit branch `fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1`)

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/19
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

## How it was tested

```
npm ci && npm run build                                        # ok
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json                # ok
npm run lint                                                   # 7/7 projects ok
cd packages/xrpl && npm test                                   # 134 suites, 1356 tests passed
```

Red before / green after: with `packages/xrpl/src` reverted to `main`, `test/models/batch.test.ts` fails to compile (`@ts-expect-error` unused, `BatchInnerTransaction` missing) and 5 of the new fee tests in `test/client/autofill.test.ts` fail; with the change all 80 tests in the three touched suites pass.

Integration, against my own standalone node (`docker run --detach --publish 6117:6006 --volume "$PWD/.ci-config/:/etc/xrpld/" --name xrpld-batch-validation-and-types rippleci/xrpld:develop --standalone`):

```
cd packages/xrpl && PORT=6117 npm run test:integration -- test/integration/transactions/batch.test.ts
# Tests: 2 passed ('base', 'batch multisign' with autofill(tx) and no signersCount -> tesSUCCESS)
```

Live fee probe on the same node with the pre-change build (base fee 200 drops): two-account Batch, old `autofill` Fee=960 -> `telINSUF_FEE_P`; Fee=1160 (one more base fee) -> `tesSUCCESS`.

The fork has no GitHub Actions runs (only Socket Security), so the local checks above are the gate.

## Follow-ups discovered (not fixed here)

- `validateBatch` still does not enforce the remaining offline-decidable rippled rules: `BatchSigners` ≤ 8, unique and ascending signer accounts, signers matching the set of inner authorizers, exactly one of `Sequence`/`TicketSequence` per inner, and no duplicate `Sequence`/`TicketSequence` per account under `tfAllOrNothing`/`tfUntilFailure` (`temREDUNDANT`).
- `signMultiBatch`'s required-signer set does not include an inner's `Sponsor` with a `SponsorSignature`, which rippled's `preflightSigValidated` requires.
- `signMultiBatch` on a flagless Batch now fails in `validate()` with a clear message instead of the bare codec error, but `encodeForSigningBatch` still binds `transaction.Flags` unconverted (object-form flags would reach the codec).
title: fix(xrpl)!: enforce Batch preflight rules, type Batch inners and Flags, fee BatchSigners

body:
## What was wrong

`Client.autofill` predates tickets and the Batch inner-transaction pass was bolted on without revisiting sequencing. Every ticket combination the sugar offers reached rippled broken: a top-level `TicketSequence` got the account's live `Sequence` injected next to it (`temSEQ_AND_TICKET`), a ticketed inner Batch transaction got no `Sequence` at all (`Field 'Sequence' is required but missing`), and a ticketed outer Batch still added `+1` to its own inner sequences, so the inner transactions failed `terPRE_SEQ` while the outer validated `tesSUCCESS` having done nothing. Independently, `autofill` shallow-copied a Batch and wrote `Sequence`/`Fee`/`SigningPubKey` into the caller's inner objects, so retrying the same Batch reused stale inner sequences (again a green `tesSUCCESS` with nothing applied), inner sequences were derived from `account_info` even when the caller pre-assigned the outer `Sequence`, and the `maxFeeXRP` cap bypass for reserve-priced types looked only at the outer `TransactionType`, capping a Batch that carries an `AccountDelete`/`AMMCreate`/`VaultCreate` below the fee the SDK itself computed.

## What changed

- `setNextValidSequenceNumber` sets `Sequence: 0` when `TicketSequence` is present instead of fetching a live sequence (086). `autofillBatchTxn` does the same for ticketed inner transactions (098).
- `autofillBatchTxn` anchors the outer account's inner sequences to the outer `Sequence`: `outer + 1` when the outer consumes a sequence, the account's next sequence when the outer is ticketed (087), and a caller-supplied outer `Sequence` is honoured (101). `Client.autofill` now settles the outer fields before the inner pass so the anchor is the value actually used.
- `autofillBatchTxn` copies the inner transaction objects before filling them, so the caller's Batch is never mutated and a retry recomputes every sequence (100).
- The fee-cap bypass applies when the outer *or any inner* transaction is reserve-priced; an inner `AccountDelete` is also checked for deletion blockers and a Batch containing one is submitted with `fail_hard` (107).
- `validateBaseTransaction` rejects a non-zero `Sequence` alongside `TicketSequence` with `BaseTransaction: Sequence must be 0 when TicketSequence is provided` (086/098).

Deviation from the finding text: 086 proposed the ticket rule inline in `Client.autofill`; it lives in `setNextValidSequenceNumber` instead so `autofill()` stays under the repo's complexity/statement lint limits and the rule sits next to the code it replaces. 101 proposed anchoring `+k` by index; the existing per-account counter already does that once seeded from the outer `Sequence`, so the seed is the only change.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/17
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Findings covered: 086, 087, 098, 100, 101, 107.

## Tests

Unit (`packages/xrpl/test/client/autofill.test.ts`): ticketed top-level → `Sequence: 0` with no `account_info` request; ticketed inner → `Sequence: 0` and no sequence consumed; ticketed outer → inner sequences start at the account sequence; outer `Sequence: 800` → inner 801/802 while another account's inner still starts at its own sequence; outer autofilled first → inner anchored to it; same Batch autofilled twice → caller's inner objects untouched and fresh sequences on the retry; inner `AccountDelete` blockers rejected; Batch containing `AccountDelete` fee'd `5000036` with a 5 XRP owner reserve (previously capped at `2000000`). The two pre-existing Batch tests encoded finding 101 (inner `24` next to a supplied outer `1432`) and now expect `Sequence + 1`. Also: `baseTransaction.test.ts` (the ticket/`Sequence` rule, and the "all optional fields" fixture no longer pairs `Sequence: 100` with `TicketSequence: 10`), `submit.test.ts` (`fail_hard` for a Batch with an inner `AccountDelete`), and the confidential Batch test's ticketed-inner assertion (`Sequence` is now `0`, not `undefined`, because `prepareConfidentialBatch` ends in `client.autofill`).

Integration (`packages/xrpl/test/integration/autofill.test.ts`, own standalone `rippleci/xrpld:develop` on port 6115): ticketed Payment, ticketed inner Batch, ticketed outer Batch and the same-object Batch retry all submit `tesSUCCESS` and each inner transaction is verified on ledger.

```
npm ci && npm run build
cd packages/xrpl && npm test                                   # 134 suites, 1351 tests passed
npm run lint                                                   # 7 packages, 0 errors, 0 warnings
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json                # clean
docker run --detach --publish 6115:6006 --volume "$PWD/.ci-config/:/etc/xrpld/" --name xrpld-autofill-tickets-and-batch-sequences rippleci/xrpld:develop --standalone
cd packages/xrpl && PORT=6115 npm run test:integration -- test/integration/autofill.test.ts                          # 4 passed
cd packages/xrpl && PORT=6115 npm run test:integration -- test/integration/transactions/batch.test.ts test/integration/transactions/accountDelete.test.ts   # 3 passed
```

Red-before-green: with `packages/xrpl/src` checked out from `main` and the new tests in place, 11 unit tests (`autofill`, `submit`, `baseTransaction`) and all 4 integration cases fail; with the fix they pass.

The fork has no GitHub Actions runs (only Socket Security checks), so the local runs above are the gate.

## Follow-ups (not fixed here)

- Whether rippled accepts `AccountDelete` as an inner Batch transaction was not verified live (XLS-56 only forbids nested `Batch`); the fee/blocker/`fail_hard` changes are harmless if it does not.
- Finding 088 (the outer Batch validating `tesSUCCESS` while every inner fails) is what made 087/100/101 silent; it belongs to its own unit.
title: fix(xrpl): autofill Sequence 0 for tickets, anchor Batch inner sequences, never mutate inner txns, uncap reserve-priced Batch fees

body:
## What was wrong

Several doc comments on the client and the MPT read/write surface were copied from neighbouring code or from spec drafts and never checked against what the code does. `Client.simulate` claimed to autofill, sign and submit when it sends the object as-is (and rippled rejects flag maps, `DeliverMax` and signed transactions). The `@example` blocks on `Client.submitAndWait` and `Wallet.sign` did not compile (undeclared `signedTransaction`, `result`, `signed_tx_blob`; un-awaited `fundWallet`) and the `submitAndWait` prose said `submit` was the one that waits. `AssetScale` was defined with inverted formulas on the transaction and ledger types, and no amount field said it is an integer in fractional units. The MPT transaction models, `Clawback`, `MPToken` and `MPTokenIssuance` had no `@category` tag so they fall out of the categorised typedoc navigation. `LockedAmount` cited payment channels, `ReferenceHolding` read as if it applied to every issuance, the `AccountObject` list predated MPT, and the `ledger_entry` MPT parameters did not say what to pass. `tfMPTCanTrade` / `tfMPTSetCanTrade` promised DEX and AMM trading that rippled 3.x answers with `temDISABLED` and that no SDK offer/AMM/book type can express, and `tfMPTSetCanClawback` promised `AMMClawback`.

## What changed

Docs only; no runtime or type changes.

- `Client.simulate`: describes the dry-run semantics and lists what the caller must do because nothing is autofilled (`Flags` numeric, no `DeliverMax`, unsigned; `Sequence`/`Fee` optional).
- `Client.submitAndWait` and `Wallet.sign` examples rewritten so they type-check against the public API (`import { Client, Payment } from 'xrpl'`, awaited `fundWallet`, `submitAndWait` actually called, `sign` fed the autofilled copy, submit inside the `try`). The prose now says `submitAndWait` waits for a validated ledger and rejects only when `LastLedgerSequence` passes; a `tec` result resolves normally.
- `AssetScale` on `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` and `MPTokenIssuance`: one definition (one standard unit = 10^AssetScale fractional units, worked example). `MPTAmount.value`, `MaximumAmount`, `OutstandingAmount`, `MPToken.MPTAmount` and both `LockedAmount` fields say "integer in fractional units of `AssetScale`".

## What was wrong

Three sharp edges on the RPC surface that an MPT issuer hits as soon as it needs to read the ledger. The Clio-only `mpt_holders` method had no request/response type, so listing the holders of an issuance did not type-check, and nothing in the SDK said that rippled cannot enumerate holders at all. `RippledError.data` was `unknown`, so telling `entryNotFound` (the "does this holder have an MPToken?" primitive) apart from any other `ledger_entry` failure needed a hand-written structural guard, and the SDK's own `waitForFinalTransactionOutcome` did the same unsafe cast. And `Client.requestAll` called `connection.request` directly, so paginated `account_tx`/`account_objects` scans silently lost the partial-payment `warnings` and the X-address conversion that `Client.request` applies.

## What changed

- **015** `models/methods/mptHolders.ts`: new `MPTHoldersRequest`, `MPTHolder`, `MPTHoldersResponse` (documented as Clio only, with the rippled `unknownCmd` behaviour spelled out). Wired into `Request`/`Response`, `RequestResponseMap` and `RequestAllResponseMap`; `requestAll` collects `mptokens`. `MPTokenIssuance` gets a `@remarks` saying rippled cannot enumerate holders.
- **035** `errors.ts`: `RippledErrorResponse` (`Partial<ErrorResponse>` plus an index signature for method-specific fields such as `index`/`ledger_index`), `RippledError.data` declared as that type, and a `RippledError.code` getter returning `data.error`. Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

No. `data` is narrowed on a subclass, the constructor signature stays compatible, and the new types are additive. `error_code` changes from `string` to `number` on `ErrorResponse`, matching runtime; nobody could have relied on the string type since rippled never sent one.

## What was wrong

Two MPT transaction-type papercuts from the audit. `Clawback` typed `Holder` as a bare `string` (and redundantly redeclared `Account: string`) while `MPTokenIssuanceSet.Holder` and `MPTokenAuthorize.Holder` use the `Account` alias, so the three MPT holder fields were not typed consistently. And `ImmutableFlags` on `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` / `MPTokenIssuanceSet` accepted only a numeric bitmask even though the SDK exports `MPTokenIssuanceCreateImmutableFlagsInterface` and every other flag field accepts the boolean-map form; `ImmutableFlags: { tifMPTCanTrade: true, tifMPTCanEscrow: true }` failed to compile (TS2322) and there was no converter, so callers had to OR the enum by hand.

## What changed

- `Clawback.Holder?: Account`; the `Account: string` redeclaration is dropped (inherited from `BaseTransaction`) and the "must be the issuer" note moved to the interface doc comment. Type-only, non-breaking (`Account` is an alias of `string`).
- `ImmutableFlags?: number | MPTokenIssuanceCreateImmutableFlagsInterface` on both `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` and `MPTokenIssuanceSet`.
- New exported `convertImmutableFlagsToNumber(flags)` (number passthrough; map → bitmask; throws `ValidationError` on a key that is not a `tif*` flag, including numeric-enum reverse-mapping keys like `"2"`). Also an internal `isImmutableFlags` type guard.
- `validateMPTokenIssuanceCreate` / `validateMPTokenIssuanceSet` accept both forms and run the existing mask / present-but-zero checks on the converted value, so `{}` or an all-`false` map is rejected exactly like an explicit `ImmutableFlags: 0` (rippled `temINVALID_FLAG`).
- `client.autofill` converts `ImmutableFlags` to a number right after it converts `Flags` (new `setImmutableFlagsToNumber` helper in `sugar/autofill.ts`), so `submit`/`simulate` send a number and the result encodes.
- Doc comments on both `ImmutableFlags` fields mention the map form; `HISTORY.md` entries under Unreleased.

**Deviation from the finding's proposed location:** the converter lives in `models/transactions/MPTokenIssuanceCreate.ts` next to the `tif*` enum and mask rather than in `models/utils/flags.ts`. `flags.ts` builds its `txToFlag` table from the transaction enums at module-evaluation time, so having `MPTokenIssuanceCreate.ts` import from `flags.ts` would add a new import cycle in which `txToFlag.MPTokenIssuanceCreate` is `undefined` whenever the transaction module is evaluated first. It is exported from the `xrpl` entry point either way.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/24
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Findings covered: 024, 034.

## How it was tested

Unit tests added in `test/models/MPTokenIssuanceCreate.test.ts` (valid map form typed without `as any`, unknown key, empty / all-false map, plus a `convertImmutableFlagsToNumber` describe block), `test/models/MPTokenIssuanceSet.test.ts` (map form, unknown `lsif*` key, empty map) and `test/client/autofill.test.ts` (Create and Set map form → `0x18` / `0x10000`, `decode(encode(...))` round-trip, numeric untouched, unknown key rejected). With the source change reverted these suites fail to compile with the finding's TS2322 (`'{ tifMPTCanTrade: true; ... }' is not assignable to type 'number'`) and the missing `convertImmutableFlagsToNumber` export; with it they pass.

npm run build
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json

npm run lint        # repo root, eslint --max-warnings 0

| `npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json` | clean |
| `npm test` in `packages/xrpl` | 134 suites, 1353 tests passed |
| `npm run lint` | exit 0 for all 7 packages, `--max-warnings 0` |

## Follow-ups discovered (not fixed here)

- `Wallet.sign` without a prior `autofill` still throws `Cannot construct UInt32 from given value` from the binary codec for the map form of `Flags`, because `validate()` normalises a copy of the transaction. `ImmutableFlags` now behaves identically (parity, not a regression); making `sign` normalise both fields is a separate change.

body:
## What was wrong

Three layers of the sign path each assumed another one checked the input. The binary codec deliberately skips unknown fields whose name starts with a lowercase letter, `validate()` had no allow-list of keys, and the encode/decode round-trip that would have caught the discrepancy was removed in 2023. So `MPTokenIssuanceSet { Flags: tfMPTLock, holder }` validated, signed, and was submitted as a lock of **every** holder (061). On top of that, `Wallet.sign` ran `removeTrailingZeros` before `validate()`, so a missing or malformed `Payment.Amount` surfaced as a raw `TypeError`, and the IOU trailing-zero helper silently canonicalised MPT values (`"10.0"` → `10`) on `Payment` only (064). Finally `validate()` converted interface-form `Flags` on a private copy while `sign` encoded the caller's object, so `Flags: { tfMPTLock: true }` passed validation and then died in the codec with `Cannot construct UInt32 from given value`; `autofillBatchTxn` had the same gap for inner transactions (065).

## What changed

- `validateBaseTransaction` (so every `validate()` caller: `Wallet.sign`, `multisign`, the Batch/sponsor/counterparty signers, and Batch inner transactions) now rejects any top-level key the binary codec does not know: `ValidationError: MPTokenIssuanceSet: unknown field "holder" (did you mean "Holder"?)`. Unknown capitalised keys (`MPTokenHolder`) get the same `ValidationError` instead of a raw codec `Error`. `DeliverMax` stays allowed on `Payment`. The check lives here rather than only in `Wallet.sign` so all signing entry points and inner Batch transactions are covered by one rule, as the sub-issue proposed.
- `Wallet.sign` runs `validate()` before `removeTrailingZeros`, and `removeTrailingZeros` skips MPT amounts. A non-canonical MPT value now fails identically on `Payment` and `Clawback` (today with the codec's `10.0 is an illegal amount`; a typed `ValidationError` for MPT value grammar belongs to the `mpt-validators` unit, #12, which will add `isMPTValue`).
- `Wallet.sign` converts interface-form `Flags` to a number before encoding (on its own copy; the caller's object is not mutated).
- `Wallet.sign` re-decodes its `tx_blob` and throws `ValidationError` if any field of the input is missing from the decoded transaction. With the unknown-field check this is a belt-and-braces guard; it is a key-presence check only, so the value rewrites that made the 2023 version brittle (trailing zeros, memo hex case, X-addresses) do not trip it.
- `autofillBatchTxn` converts inner `Flags` and folds inner `DeliverMax` into `Amount`, mirroring what `Client.autofill` already did for the outer transaction.
- Two existing test fixtures were exactly the bug class: `SigningPublicKey` in the base-transaction test and lowercase `flags` in the AMMClawback `tfClawTwoAssets` test (which therefore never exercised the flag). Fixed both.
- Changelog entries under `packages/xrpl/HISTORY.md` Unreleased.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/14
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Findings covered: 061, 064, 065.

## Behaviour note (not breaking, but visible)

`validate()` is public. It now throws on keys such as `meta`, `date`, `ledger_index`, `validated` or `ctid`, so calling it on a raw `tx` RPC result object (rather than a transaction you intend to sign) no longer passes. Nothing in the SDK or its test suite did this; the codec would have rejected or dropped those keys anyway.

## How it was tested

Fork has no Actions runs (only Socket Security checks), so local checks are the gate.

```
npm ci && npm run build                                              # ok
cd packages/xrpl && npx jest --config=jest.config.unit.js            # 134 suites, 1352 tests passed
npm run lint                                                         # 7 projects, clean (--max-warnings 0)
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json                      # clean
```

The 11 new tests (`test/wallet/index.test.ts`, `test/models/baseTransaction.test.ts`, `test/client/autofill.test.ts`) were run against unpatched `src/` first: 11 failed, then all pass with the fix.

Acceptance criteria from the sub-issue:
- `sign({ ...set, holder })` throws `ValidationError: MPTokenIssuanceSet: unknown field "holder" (did you mean "Holder"?)` ✔
- `sign(payment without Amount)` throws `PaymentTransaction: missing field Amount`, not a `TypeError` ✔
- `sign({ ...set, Flags: { tfMPTLock: true } })` succeeds with numeric flags on the wire; a Batch with inner object `Flags` autofills to numeric ✔
- MPT `value: '10.0'` rejected identically on `Payment` and `Clawback` ✔ (same error message asserted)
- `audit/mpt-issuer` scenario: run from the audit branch against this branch's built package on my own standalone `rippleci/xrpld:develop` container (port 6112, removed afterwards): **63/63 passed**.

No ledger-side behaviour changed, so no new integration test was added.

## Follow-ups noticed (not fixed here)

- `Holder: undefined` on `MPTokenIssuanceSet` is still stripped by `omitBy` before validation and signs as a global lock (finding 061, round-3 note). An issuer-side guard or a builder taking `holder: string` is the fix; not in this unit.
- `Wallet.sign` does not fold `DeliverMax` into `Amount` for offline signing; only `autofill` does. Offline `Payment { DeliverMax }` without `Amount` still fails with `missing field Amount` (unchanged).
- A typed `ValidationError` for MPT value grammar (`"10.0"`, `"1e3"`, values above 2^63-1) is left to `mpt-validators` (#12).
title: fix(xrpl): harden the sign path against unknown fields, amount rewrites and object Flags

## What was wrong

Several error paths in `xrpl` reported problems through the wrong channel or with misleading text. The MPT metadata validators (`MPTokenIssuanceCreate`, `MPTokenIssuanceSet`, and the same block in `VaultCreate`) called `console.warn` from inside `validate()`, so every `Wallet.sign`/`submit` of a token with non-XLS-89 metadata wrote untagged multi-line output to stderr with no way to capture or silence it, and `Client.getServerInfo` swallowed a failed `server_info` with `console.error`, leaving `networkID` undefined silently. The `AccountDelete` autofill blocker message hard-coded "Escrows, PayChannels, RippleStates, Checks, or Sponsorships" even when the actual blockers were `MPTokenIssuance`/`MPToken` entries, and the owner-reserve fetch threw a plain `Error`. Flag-conversion errors named no transaction type and dumped `JSON.stringify` of a numeric enum (including its reverse mappings); `fundWallet` threw `RippledError` for "not connected" although `NotConnectedError` exists; `UnexpectedError`/`RippledNotInitializedError` are exported but never thrown; the Batch inner-transaction rules were enforced with `XrplError` and a stray backtick in `autofill` but `ValidationError` in `validate`; and `Wallet.sign`'s `@throws` documented an encode/decode check removed in 2023.

## What changed

- **027** `MPTokenIssuanceCreate`/`MPTokenIssuanceSet`/`VaultCreate`: removed the `console.warn` blocks. `validateMPTokenMetadata` stays the (now documented) advisory API; `MPT_META_WARNING_HEADER` is still exported for callers who want the ready-made explanation. `Client.getServerInfo()` now rejects when `server_info` fails; `Client.connect()` catches that, emits the client's existing `error` event with code `'server_info'`, and still resolves (non-breaking: the client is an eventemitter3 emitter, so an unhandled `error` event does not throw).
- **067** `checkAccountDeleteBlockers` now lists the actual `LedgerEntryType`s with counts, e.g. `... it still owns deletion-blocking ledger entries: MPTokenIssuance (1), MPToken (2).`, keeping the `account_objects` array in `err.data`. `fetchOwnerReserveFee` throws `XrplError` naming the missing `server_state.validated_ledger.reserve_inc` field (the finding's text mentioned `server_info.reserve_inc_xrp`; the code reads `server_state`, so the message follows the code).
- **069** `convertTxFlagsToNumber` errors read `<TransactionType>: invalid flag "<flag>". Valid flags: a, b, c` and list only string keys (reverse enum entries filtered out); the two code paths collapsed into one. `fundWallet` throws `NotConnectedError`. `UnexpectedError` and `RippledNotInitializedError` are marked `@deprecated` rather than deleted, because deleting an exported class is a breaking change and this unit is non-breaking; removal can land in the next major. Batch inner-rule violations in `autofillBatchTxn` are now `ValidationError`s naming `RawTransactions[i].RawTransaction.<Field>` like `validate()` does (`ValidationError extends XrplError`, so existing `catch (XrplError)` code keeps working). `Wallet.sign`'s `@throws` rewritten to what it actually throws.
- `packages/xrpl/HISTORY.md`: entries under Unreleased (Fixed + Deprecated).

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/25
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Findings covered: 027, 067, 069.

## How it was tested

```
npm ci && npm run build                                  # ok
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json          # no errors
npm run lint                                             # Successfully ran target lint for 7 projects
cd packages/xrpl && npm test                             # 135 suites, 1348 tests passed
```

New/updated unit tests (13), all red on the unfixed source and green after the fix (verified by reverting `src/` and re-running):

- `test/models/MPTokenIssuanceCreate.test.ts`, `MPTokenIssuanceSet.test.ts`, `vaultCreate.test.ts`: `validate()` with non-XLS-89 metadata writes nothing to `console.warn/error/log`; `validateMPTokenMetadata` still returns the messages.
- `test/client/getServerInfo.test.ts` (new): `getServerInfo()` rejects with `RippledError` when `server_info` errors; `connect()` still resolves and emits `error` with code `'server_info'`; nothing on the console.
- `test/client/autofill.test.ts`: AccountDelete blocker message contains `MPTokenIssuance (1), MPToken (2)` and `err.data` carries the objects; missing `reserve_inc` rejects with `XrplError`; Batch inner `Fee`/`TxnSignature` violations reject with `ValidationError` and the field path.
- `test/models/utils.test.ts`: flag error text for a type-specific enum, for `Clawback` given an `MPTokenIssuanceSet` flag, and for a type with only global flags.
- `test/wallet/fundWallet.test.ts`: not-connected client rejects with `NotConnectedError`.

No integration test: this unit changes error classes, messages and reporting channels only, not behaviour against the ledger, so no standalone node was started.

## Follow-ups noticed (not fixed here)

- `sugar/autofill.ts` still has two `console.warn` calls (`calculateSponsorFee`, the LoanSet counterparty-signer fee note) and `models/utils/flags.ts` has the `setTransactionFlagsToNumber` deprecation `console.warn`. Same channel problem as 027 but outside this unit's findings; a client-level `warnings` channel would cover all of them.
- `validateBatchInnerTransaction` (`models/transactions/batch.ts`) still reports `Batch: invalid field RawTransactions[i].RawTransaction.Fee` without saying what the value must be; aligning its text with the autofill message would finish the unification (file not in this unit's scope).

body:
## What was wrong

The MPT transaction doc comments lagged the protocol and the SDK's own validators. `MPTokenAuthorize` carried the `MPTokenIssuanceSet` lock/unlock text verbatim, so it described a different transaction. `MPTokenIssuanceSet` documented only lock/unlock and did not say that `tfMPTSet*` flags are one-way, that `Holder` is lock-only, or what a lock actually does to payments (issuer-direction payments and `Clawback` still work). `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` claimed it was "the only opportunity" to set flags (false under DynamicMPT unless pinned with `ImmutableFlags`), that `TransferFee` "must NOT be present" without `tfMPTCanTransfer` (0 is accepted by the validator and by rippled), and that `MaximumAmount` is "non-negative" (`'0'` is rejected). `MPTokenIssuance.Sequence` said it equals the account `Sequence`, but for ticketed creates it is the `TicketSequence`, which changes the derived `MPTokenIssuanceID`. `ConfidentialMPTClawback.MPTAmount` read as a partial amount while the builder documents all-or-nothing, and nothing on `Clawback` said a confidential balance is out of its reach.

## What changed

Docs only in `packages/xrpl/src/models`, plus one validator test and a HISTORY line.

- `MPTokenAuthorize.ts`: interface, `Holder` and `tfMPTUnauthorize` rewritten for the two roles (holder opt-in/opt-out, issuer authorize/unauthorize), with the engine results the issuer project hit: `tecDUPLICATE`, `tecHAS_OBLIGATIONS`, `tecNO_PERMISSION` for a locked opt-out, `tecOBJECT_NOT_FOUND` before opt-in, `tecNO_AUTH` on an issuance without `lsfMPTRequireAuth`.
- `MPTokenIssuanceSet.ts`: interface doc lists all five kinds of change and the `Holder` combination rules the validator enforces. `tfMPTLock`/`tfMPTUnlock` now state the payment effect (holder-to-holder `tecLOCKED`, issuer-direction and `Clawback` unaffected), lock/auth independence and precedence, idempotency, the pinned-reserve consequence, and the `tecPATH_PARTIAL` ordering. Every `tfMPTSet*` member (enum and interface) says "one-way". The interface's `/* */` comments became `/** */` so editors and typedoc show them. `tfMPTSetCanHoldConfidentialBalance` states the `Clawback` consequence. `DomainID` states the `lsfMPTRequireAuth` precondition and that the zero hash clears (verified in rippled `MPTokenIssuanceSet.cpp` preclaim/doApply).

## What was wrong

The holder-side `MPToken` ledger type was modelled but never joined to the `LedgerEntry` union (nor were `DID`, `NFTokenOffer`, `NFTokenPage`), so a `LedgerEntryType === 'MPToken'` check never narrowed and every read of a holder's balance or flags needed `as unknown as MPToken`. The type itself also disagreed with rippled's `ltMPTOKEN` template: it lacked the always-present `Account`, marked `MPTAmount` required although rippled omits it when zero, and marked `OwnerNode` optional. `MPTokenIssuance` lacked the synthetic `mpt_issuance_id` rippled injects on every JSON view of the entry. There was no `lsfMPT*` enum or parser for the holder entry (unlike the issuance), `Credential.Flags` carried a transaction-style `number | object` union the ledger never returns, and the `lsfAccepted` bit value appeared nowhere in the SDK. Finally, ledger-entry types were only reachable as `LedgerEntry.X`; `import { MPToken } from 'xrpl'` failed with a misleading "did you mean MPTokenIssuanceSet" suggestion and the repo's own tests deep-imported instead.

## What changed

- `LedgerEntry` union: add `MPToken`, `DID`, `NFTokenOffer`, `NFTokenPage` (`models/ledger/LedgerEntry.ts`). Every `LedgerEntryFilter` now has a union member; a compile-time `Record<LedgerEntryFilter, LedgerEntry['LedgerEntryType']>` in the new unit test enforces that going forward.
- `MPToken`: add `Account: string`, make `MPTAmount` optional, make `OwnerNode` required, document the fields; add `MPTokenFlags` enum (`lsfMPTLocked = 0x1`, `lsfMPTAuthorized = 0x2`) and `MPTokenFlagsInterface`.
- `MPTokenIssuance`: add `mpt_issuance_id: string` (documented as rippled-injected, not stored on the ledger).
- `Credential`: `Flags: number`; the old unexported `CredentialFlags` interface becomes `CredentialFlagsInterface`, and `CredentialFlags` is now an enum with `lsfAccepted = 0x00010000`.
- `models/utils/flags.ts`: add `parseMPTokenFlags` and `parseCredentialFlags`, same shape as `parseMPTokenIssuanceFlags`; both exported at the package root.
- `models/index.ts`: keep the `LedgerEntry` namespace and additionally re-export every ledger-entry name that does not collide with an existing root export. The collision set was determined by compiling with a temporary `export * from './ledger'` at the root: only `DepositPreauth` (transaction), `NFToken` (common type) and `LedgerEntry` (the namespace) collide, so everything else is now importable as `import { MPToken, MPTokenIssuance, AccountRoot, ... } from 'xrpl'`.
- Integration tests: drop the four `@ts-expect-error: Known issue with unknown object type` lines in `clawback.test.ts` and `mptokenIssuanceCreate.test.ts` (they now narrow with `assert(node.LedgerEntryType === 'MPToken')`), drop the `(node as { mpt_issuance_id?: string })` cast in `mptokenIssuanceSet.test.ts`, and switch both MPT test files from deep imports to the root import.
- `HISTORY.md`: entries under Unreleased (Added / Fixed).

Deviations from the finding files: finding 010 also suggested a `getMPTokenBalance` helper; not added here to keep the unit type-only (see follow-ups). Finding 031 offered a README paragraph as an alternative; the root re-export makes it unnecessary.

Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

No exported symbol is removed. `MPTAmount` becoming optional can surface new `string | undefined` errors in callers that assumed it was always present; those callers were already wrong at runtime for zero-balance holders. `mpt_issuance_id` becoming a required field of `MPTokenIssuance` only affects code that constructs issuance literals by hand (tests); every RPC view carries it.

## What was wrong

The codec accepted several inputs that were never encoded as written. `hexToBytes` silently dropped a trailing odd nibble (node) or floored the byte count (browser), so a `CredentialType: 'ABC'` signed locally stored `AB` while `simulate`/JSON submit stored `0ABC`, and a 49-character `MPTokenIssuanceID` was accepted and shifted onto a different issuance. `Hash192.from('')` and `AccountID.from('')` quietly encoded the all-zero issuance ID and `rrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrhoLvTp`. `Issue.from({ currency: 'USD', issuer: '' })` took the XRP branch and emitted a 20-byte blob that the codec could not decode back. And when a field did fail, the error said `Invalid Function: 256 must be >= 0 and <= 255`, reported a base-10 `MaximumAmount` overflow as a bad hex string, or surfaced a raw `TypeError` with no field name.

## What changed

- **`@xrplf/isomorphic`** `hexToBytes` / `hexToString` (node and browser builds) throw `Invalid hex string: odd length (N)` on odd-length input. Every codec hex sink goes through this, so `Blob`, `Hash*`, `Currency` and the rest all reject odd-length hex with no per-type changes.
- **`Hash192`** no longer zero-fills an empty input; `Hash192.from('')` throws `Invalid Hash length 0` like `Hash256` already did.
- **`AccountID.from('')`** throws and points at the explicit base58 form for ACCOUNT_ZERO. This drops the 2020 pseudo-transaction convenience ("Blank AccountID is ACCOUNT_ZERO"); `decode` never produced `''` (the sibling test expected `rrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrrhoLvTp`), and xrpl 2.13.0's changelog already declared `''` invalid for address fields, so only the codec was out of step. The pseudo-transaction tests now assert the throw and the base58 round-trip.
- **`Issue.from`** decides XRP via `Currency.iso() === 'XRP'` (so the 40-zero hex form still works) and throws `Issue: issuer is required for non-XRP currency USD` for a missing **or** empty issuer. The audit proposed checking only `issuer: ''`; a missing issuer produces the same malformed blob through the same branch, so both are covered by one check.
- **`UInt.checkUintRange`** uses `this.name` (the concrete class when called as `UInt8.checkUintRange`) instead of `this.constructor.name`, which is `"Function"` in a static method.
- **`UInt64.from`** checks the base-10 value against 2^64-1 before converting to hex, so the error reads `MaximumAmount 18446744073709551616 exceeds 2^64-1`.
- **`STObject.from`** wraps per-field construction in a try/catch and prefixes the field name (`AssetScale: Invalid UInt8: 256 must be >= 0 and <= 255`, `Memos: Memo: MemoData: Invalid hex string: odd length (3)`). Messages that already start with the field name (the UInt64 base-10 errors) pass through unchanged.
- **`Amount.assertMptIsValid`** rejects a non-string `value` with `MPT amount value must be a decimal string, got number` instead of `amount.indexOf is not a function` (listed in finding 097's affected surface).
- Changelog lines under `Unreleased` in `packages/isomorphic/HISTORY.md` and `packages/ripple-binary-codec/HISTORY.md`.

Not breaking in the sense of the sub-issue: every rejected input was previously encoded as something other than what the caller wrote. One test in `packages/xrpl` anchored a regex at the start of a codec message and was updated for the new `Amount:` prefix.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/11
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

All pass with the fix.

cd packages/isomorphic && npx jest ./test/*.test.ts                 # 4 suites, 18 tests, all pass
cd packages/ripple-binary-codec && npx jest ./test/*.test.ts        # 20 suites, 1311 tests, all pass

- `Hash128.from('')` still zero-fills. It is deliberate (`EmailHash` "unset" semantics, `toHex()` returns `''` for all zeros) and outside this unit; left as is.
- `UInt64.from(bigint)` above 2^64-1 still truncates silently (audit finding 022, a different unit).
- `Issue.from({ currency: 'XRP', issuer: 'r...' })` still serialises a 40-byte Issue that rippled will reject; `isIssueObject` accepts the shape. Adjacent to 095 but not in its findings.
- An empty `mpt_issuance_id` inside an `Amount` reports `Amount: Invalid Hash length 0` without naming the sub-key.
- The `xrpl`-side guards (`isHex` parity, `isAccount` on `Account`/`Subject`/`Issuer`, `isMPTokenIssuanceID`) belong to the validator units per the plan.

body:
## What was wrong

`Amount.assertMptIsValid` in `ripple-binary-codec` tested only bit 63 of the MPT `value`, so any value at or above 2^64 with bit 63 clear passed and the two `writeUInt32BE` calls serialized its low 64 bits: `"18446744073709551621"` (2^64 + 5) encoded as `5`, 2^64 and 2^65 as `0`, with no error. The same function validated with `BigNumber` and then `BigInt`, whose grammars accept `"0x10"`, `"+7"` and `" 9"` (silently reinterpreted as 16, 7, 9) and throw a raw `SyntaxError` for `"1e2"`. In the same family, `UInt32.from(string)` was an unchecked `parseInt` (`"-1"` -> 4294967295, `"4294967296"` -> 0), `UInt64.from(number)` accepted numbers above `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` (`1e20`, `2^53 + 1` lose precision) and `UInt64.from(bigint)` truncated at 2^64. All of these are reachable through `encode` / `encodeForSigning` and `client.submit(preSignedObject)`, which do not run `validate()`. The codec's MPT error fixtures asserted a bare `toThrow()` and stopped at 2^64 - 1, so the range bug sat next to a test named "Value is too large".

## What changed

- `src/types/amount.ts`: `assertMptIsValid` now accepts exactly the canonical decimal form `/^(?:0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/` and requires `BigInt(value) <= 2^63 - 1`. Everything else (sign, whitespace, `0x`/`0o`/`0b` prefix, exponent, decimal point, leading zeros, empty string, non-string) throws the codec's own `Error("<value> is an illegal amount")`, the same message as before. The bit-63 `mptMask` check is gone.
- `src/types/uint-32.ts`: the string path requires `/^[0-9]{1,10}$/` and runs the same `checkUintRange` as the number path.
- `src/types/uint-64.ts`: `number` inputs must satisfy `Number.isSafeInteger`; `bigint` inputs must be in `0..2^64 - 1`. Also drops a redundant `Number(Number(...))`.
- `test/fixtures/data-driven-tests.json`: adds error vectors for 2^64, 2^64 + 5, 2^65, `"0x10"`, `"+7"`, `" 9"`, `"1e2"`, `"007"` and `""`; relabels the four hex-flavoured labels ("Hex value out of range" etc.) to say why they are rejected; converts the three positive vectors `"-0"`, `"0xa"`, `"0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF"` into error vectors.
- `test/amount.test.ts`: the data-driven error runner now maps every fixture `error` label to the expected message and asserts the thrown value is a plain `Error` (never a leaked `SyntaxError`/`TypeError`) whose message matches; an unmapped label fails the test. Adds direct round-trip and rejection tables for 022/023.
- `test/uint.test.ts`: string/number/bigint cases for UInt32/UInt64 plus `encode`-level cases for `Sequence` and `MaximumAmount`.
- `HISTORY.md`: three `### Fixed` lines under Unreleased.

### Deliberate decision on `0x` MPT values (finding 023 note)

The existing fixtures expected in-range `0x…` values (and `"-0"`) to encode, which implies hex was once meant to be accepted. This PR rejects them. Reasons: the sub-issue's acceptance criteria list `"0x10"` as a value `encode` must throw for; the JSON form of an MPT amount is documented as a base 10 decimal string and that is the only form rippled emits; and accepting hex here is exactly the reinterpretation hazard 023 describes (`"0x10"` is worth sixteen times what a reader of the JSON assumes). Flagging it explicitly because it is the one input class that previously encoded correctly and no longer does; it is not a wire-compatibility change.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/10
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Findings covered: 022, 023, 096, 085.

## How it was tested

Red before the fix: with the new tests in place and `src/` reverted to `main`, `jest test/amount.test.ts test/uint.test.ts` fails 17 of 79 (the truncation, non-canonical string, `UInt32` string and `UInt64` number/bigint cases). Green after:

```
npm ci && npm run build                          # ok
packages/ripple-binary-codec: npm test           # 19 suites, 1297 tests passed
packages/ripple-binary-codec: npm run lint       # clean
packages/xrpl: npm test                          # 134 suites, 1339 tests passed
npm run lint (root, all packages)                # clean
```

The fork has no CI checks configured (no workflow runs exist on theahaco/xrpl.js), so the local runs above are the gate.

No ledger-runtime behaviour changes (serialization-time validation only), so no integration test was added or run.

## Follow-ups discovered (not fixed here)

- The out-of-range message for `UInt32.from('4294967296')` comes from `UInt.checkUintRange` and reads `Invalid Function: 4294967296 must be >= 0 and <= 4294967295` (`this.constructor.name` inside a static method). That is finding 097 and is left as is; the new string path reuses `checkUintRange` on purpose so both paths change together when 097 lands.
- `encode({ MaximumAmount: "18446744073709551616" })` still reports the value in hex (`10000000000000000 is not a valid hex-string`) because the base 10 to hex conversion happens before the length check; also 097.

body:
## What was wrong

Two validators in `packages/xrpl` were stricter than rippled, so `Wallet.sign` (which calls `validate`) rejected transactions the ledger accepts. `isDomainID` rejects the all-zero hash on every transaction, but on `MPTokenIssuanceSet` an all-zero `DomainID` is exactly how rippled removes the domain from an issuance (`sle->makeFieldAbsent(sfDomainID)`), so the SDK could not express "clear the domain" without a manual signing path. `validateCredentialCreate` applied rippled's 256-byte `URI` limit (`maxCredentialURILength`) to the hex-encoded string, halving the effective limit to 128 bytes and quoting the wrong number in the error; the unit test codified the bug. `DIDSet.URI`, which has the same 256-byte limit in rippled, had no length check at all.

## What changed

- `common.ts`: new `isDomainIDOrZero` (64 hex chars, zero allowed). `isDomainID` is now defined in terms of it plus the non-zero check, so `Payment`, `OfferCreate` and `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` keep the strict guard unchanged.
- `MPTokenIssuanceSet.ts`: validate `DomainID` with `isDomainIDOrZero`; field doc says all zeros removes the domain. Side effect: an all-zero `DomainID` combined with `Holder` now reports the intended "Cannot set both DomainID and Holder fields" message instead of "invalid field DomainID".
- `CredentialCreate.ts`: `MAX_URI_LENGTH` is now `256 * 2` hex characters; the error message states both the hex and byte limits; the `URI` field doc states the limit.
- `DIDSet.ts`: reject `URI` longer than 512 hex characters (256 bytes), matching rippled's `maxDIDURILength`. Empty string stays allowed because rippled uses it to clear the field.
- `HISTORY.md`: two lines under Unreleased / Fixed.

Non-breaking: every change accepts input that rippled accepts, and the only new rejection (`DIDSet.URI` over 256 bytes) is a transaction rippled would return `temMALFORMED` for.

Fixes https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/15
Part of https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/issues/2

Findings covered: 038, 071.

## How it was tested

Unit tests were written first and reproduced all three bugs red (5 failures) before the source change:

- `test/models/MPTokenIssuanceSet.test.ts`: all-zero `DomainID` accepted; wrong-length and non-hex still rejected; all-zero `DomainID` + `Holder` gives the "Cannot set both" message.
- `test/models/CredentialCreate.test.ts`: 256-byte URI accepted; too-long test moved from 129 to 257 bytes with the new message.
- `test/models/DIDSet.test.ts`: 256-byte URI accepted; 257 bytes rejected.

Integration tests (per the sub-issue acceptance criteria) against my own standalone `rippleci/xrpld:develop` container on port 6113:

- `mptokenIssuanceSet.test.ts` "clears DomainID on the MPTokenIssuance ledger object via an all-zero DomainID": create with `tfMPTRequireAuth` + domain, set `'0'.repeat(64)` through `submitAndWait`, read the entry back, `DomainID` is absent.
- `credentialCreate.test.ts` "accepts a URI longer than 128 bytes (rippled allows 256)": 200-byte URI signed through `Wallet.sign`, `tesSUCCESS`, `URI` round-trips on the `Credential` entry.

GitHub Actions has never run on this fork (zero workflow runs, and this PR shows no checks), so the gate is the local checks below rather than CI.

Commands and results:

```
npm ci && npm run build                                   # ok
cd packages/xrpl && npm test                              # 134 suites, 1346 tests passed
npm run lint (root)                                       # clean, 0 warnings
npx tsc --noEmit -p packages/xrpl/tsconfig.json           # clean
docker run --detach --publish 6113:6006 --volume "$PWD/.ci-config/:/etc/xrpld/" \
  --name xrpld-over-strict-validators rippleci/xrpld:develop --standalone
PORT=6113 npm run test:integration -- test/integration/transactions/mptokenIssuanceSet.test.ts \
  test/integration/transactions/credentialCreate.test.ts test/integration/transactions/didSet.test.ts
                                                          # 3 suites, 15 tests passed
docker rm -f xrpld-over-strict-validators
```

## Follow-ups discovered (not fixed here)

- The sub-issue's third acceptance criterion (drop `signBypassingValidate` from `audit/mpt-issuer/src/domain.ts`) lives under `audit/`, which belongs to https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/1 and is out of scope for this PR. Once this lands, that helper is no longer needed for the domain-clear and long-URI probes.
- `DIDSet.Data` and `DIDSet.DIDDocument` have the same 256-byte limits in rippled (`maxDIDAttestationLength`, `maxDIDDocumentLength`) and still have no client-side length check. Only `URI` was in this unit's scope.
- The 300-byte credential URI rejection is covered by the unit test (257 bytes) rather than an integration test, since the rejection is client-side and never reaches the node.

## Executive summary

- **107 findings**: 2 blockers, 24 major, 60 minor, 21 paper-cuts (table below). Round 1 (building
  the issuer) produced 42; round 2 (five adversarial sweeps, every candidate re-verified on the
  ledger or against the built package) produced 38; round 3 (four more sweeps: the repo's tests as
  evidence, the codec's MPT paths, cross-feature interactions, and a dry-run repeat of the core
  lenses) produced 17; round 4 (two dry-run sweeps with all 97 findings as exclusions) produced 2,
  both on the Batch surface, and the second sweep produced nothing beyond them; round 5 (one
  targeted pass over the Batch/ticket/signing surface, the only area still yielding) produced 4,
  three of them major; round 6 (a general user-journey pass and a second targeted Batch pass)
  produced 0 and 2 minor; round 7 (a third targeted Batch pass) produced 1 minor and 1 paper-cut.
  **Stopping point**: the general MPT surface returned nothing new in two consecutive sweeps
  (rounds 4 and 6); the Batch/ticket/signing surface, which the audit's scope only touched in
  passing, still yields but with strictly falling severity (major → minor → paper-cut) — it
  deserves its own audit rather than more passes here.
- **Batch is the least trustworthy part of the SDK for an issuer**: beyond the ticket bugs, a
  retried Batch object reuses stale inner sequences and reports `tesSUCCESS` having done nothing
  ([100](100-autofill-mutates-inner-batch-transactions-stale-retry.md), reproduced live), a
  pre-assigned outer `Sequence` is ignored for the inners ([101](101-batch-inner-sequences-ignore-caller-supplied-outer-sequence.md)),
  and a multisig issuer cannot co-sign at all because `combineBatchSigners` drops all but one
  co-signature ([102](102-combinebatchsigners-drops-multisign-fragments-per-account.md)).
- **The ticket path is broken at every level**: `autofill` injects a live `Sequence` next to a
  caller's `TicketSequence` (`temSEQ_AND_TICKET`, [086](086-autofill-injects-sequence-next-to-ticketsequence.md)),
  a ticketed inner Batch transaction is emitted with no `Sequence` at all (`invalidTransaction`,
  [098](098-batch-autofill-emits-ticketed-inner-without-sequence.md)), and a ticketed outer
  `Batch` gets inner sequences off by one so the outer reports `tesSUCCESS` while none of the
  inner locks applied ([087](087-batch-autofill-off-by-one-under-ticketed-outer.md),
  [088](088-batch-outcome-silent-no-inner-results.md)). Tickets and batches are exactly what an
  issuer reaches for to get an emergency freeze out atomically, and rippled's `simulate` cannot
  dry-run a `Batch` ([099](099-validatebatch-misses-mode-flag-and-count-rules.md)).
- **Two blockers put a different transaction on the wire than the developer wrote, with no error
  from any layer**: the binary codec encodes an MPT `value` of 2^64 + 5 as **5**
  ([022](022-binary-codec-silently-truncates-mpt-values-above-2-64.md)), and a lowercase field name
  such as `holder` is silently dropped when signing, so a per-holder lock becomes a **global freeze
  of every holder** ([061](061-lowercase-field-names-silently-dropped-when-signing.md)). Both fixes
  are a few lines.
- **`submitAndWait` can report a validated transaction as expired** ("Preliminary result:
  tesSUCCESS") because it checks `LastLedgerSequence` before its final `tx` lookup
  ([062](062-submitandwait-expiry-check-precedes-final-tx-lookup.md), reproduced live); an operator
  who retries claws back twice.
- **The two "balances" helpers do not know MPTs exist**: `getBalances` returns only XRP for a holder
  with 100 units ([077](077-getbalances-omits-mpt-holdings.md)) and `getBalanceChanges` reports only
  the XRP fee for an MPT payment or clawback ([053](053-getbalancechanges-ignores-mpt-nodes.md)).
- **The four captain's requirements are achievable, with one honest caveat**: "pre-emptively ban an
  address" has no on-ledger representation. The closest model (allow-listing + never authorize +
  lock-on-arrival + lock-and-clawback for current holders) is implemented in `mpt-issuer/src/ban.ts`
  and proven in the scenario; the limits are in [028](028-pre-emptive-ban-not-expressible-on-ledger.md).
- **The scenario is green**: `npm run scenario` → 63/63 assertions pass on rippled 3.4.0-rc1
  (`rippleci/xrpld:develop`).
- **The type-level seeds from the captain's notes all reproduce** ([001](001-submitandwait-meta-string-undefined.md)–[005](005-ledger-entry-response-never-narrows-node.md)),
  and they compound: because [006](006-mptoken-missing-from-ledgerentry-union.md) leaves `MPToken`
  out of the `LedgerEntry` union, the holder-side read path is unreachable without `as unknown as`,
  which the repo's own tests acknowledge with `@ts-expect-error`.
- **Client-side validation is thin exactly where MPTs are new, and over-strict twice**: `validate()`
  accepts every malformed MPT amount, unknown flag bit, odd-length hex and any string as an ID
  ([016](016-mpt-amount-value-not-validated-no-scale-helper.md), [037](037-mpt-validators-do-not-check-flag-masks.md),
  [070](070-odd-length-hex-truncated-on-signed-path.md), [036](036-mptokenissuanceid-format-not-validated.md)),
  while rejecting the zero `DomainID` that clears a domain
  ([038](038-isdomainid-rejects-zero-hash-that-clears-domain.md)) and credential URIs over 128 bytes
  that rippled accepts up to 256 ([071](071-credentialcreate-uri-capped-at-half-rippled-limit.md)).
- **Every forced cast, `!`, or `@ts-expect-error` in `mpt-issuer/` is tagged `AUDIT-NNN`** in a
  comment; `grep -rn AUDIT- mpt-issuer/src` lists them.

## Design mapping: requirement → ledger mechanism → xrpl.js calls

| Requirement | Ledger mechanism | xrpl.js | Achievable as stated? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1. Clawback | `MPTokenIssuanceCreate` with `tfMPTCanClawback`; `Clawback { Amount: { mpt_issuance_id, value }, Holder }` | `mpt-issuer/src/ban.ts` `clawbackTx`, `clawback.ts` | **Yes.** Works while the holder is locked, unauthorized, and during a global freeze; claws back `min(value, balance)`; empty holder → `tecINSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`; no MPToken → `tecOBJECT_NOT_FOUND`. |
| 2. Pre-emptive ban | `tfMPTRequireAuth` (allow-list). A never-authorized address cannot receive (`tecNO_AUTH`). **Nothing can be written on-ledger for an address that has not opted in** (`MPTokenAuthorize`/`MPTokenIssuanceSet` with `Holder` → `tecOBJECT_NOT_FOUND`), and opt-in cannot be prevented. | `ban.ts` `banAddress` (local registry) + `authorizeUnlessBanned` (guard) + `sweepBanned` (lock-on-arrival) | **Not as stated.** Closest: off-ledger registry + refuse to authorize + lock the empty MPToken the moment it appears. rippled cannot enumerate holders (`mpt_holders` is Clio-only), so the sweep polls `ledger_entry` per banned address. Alternative: permissioned-domain admission (`DomainID` + credentials), where "ban" = never issue / revoke the credential (`CredentialDelete` blocks send and receive but leaves the balance); still not pre-emptive, cannot be combined with `Holder`. See [028](028-pre-emptive-ban-not-expressible-on-ledger.md). |
| 3. Freeze newly banned accounts | `MPTokenIssuanceSet { Holder, Flags: tfMPTLock }` sets `lsfMPTLocked` on the holder's `MPToken`. Requires `tfMPTCanLock` on the issuance. | `freeze.ts` `holderLock`, used by `ban.ts` | **Yes**, once the MPToken exists. Lock works on a zero-balance unauthorized entry, survives a later (mistaken) authorization (`tecLOCKED` beats auth), blocks holder↔holder both ways. Caveats: issuer↔holder payments are still allowed under a per-holder lock; a locked holder can never delete its entry. Clawback is unaffected, so "ban" = lock + clawback in one call. |
| 4. Global freeze | `MPTokenIssuanceSet { Flags: tfMPTLock }` (no `Holder`) sets `lsfMPTLocked` on the `MPTokenIssuance`; `tfMPTUnlock` clears it. | `freeze.ts` `globalLock`/`globalUnlock`; verified via `parseMPTokenIssuanceFlags` | **Yes**, with the same exemption: holder↔holder payments fail with `tecLOCKED`, but the issuer can still pay holders and holders can still redeem to the issuer. Idempotent. Per-holder locks are independent bits and survive a global unlock. |

Immutability: the issuer pins `ImmutableFlags = tifMPTCanTrade | tifMPTCanEscrow |
tifMPTCanHoldConfidentialBalance` (capabilities that must never be switched on later; `tfMPTSet*`
are one-way *on*, so this is the only way to promise holders the token will not become
tradable/escrowable/confidential) plus the three safety flags for documentation value. Verified:
`tfMPTSetCanTrade` on the pinned issuance → `tecNO_PERMISSION`. (MPT trading is `temDISABLED` on
this rippled anyway, [052](052-cantrade-docs-promise-dex-amm-the-sdk-cannot-express.md).)


## How to run the issuer project

```sh
npm ci && npm run build                         # repo root; produces packages/xrpl/dist
cd audit/mpt-issuer && npm install              # links xrpl -> ../../packages/xrpl (file:)
npm run typecheck                               # strict tsc over src/ (no any, every cast tagged)
npm run type-repros                             # compiles src/type-repros/repros.ts: passes only while the type findings exist
npm run check-amendments                        # behavioural amendment probe
npm run scenario                                # the end-to-end lifecycle, prints a PASS/FAIL table, exit 1 on any failure
npm run issue | holders | ban | freeze | clawback | domain | probes   # individual modules
npm run inspect -- <MPTokenIssuanceID> [holder] # read-side helpers, keylet derivation, mpt_holders attempt
```

`XRPL_URL` (default `ws://localhost:6006`) and `LEDGER_TICK_MS` are configurable. The scenario
prints the realpath `xrpl` resolves to (`packages/xrpl/dist/npm/index.js`) as proof that the local
build is what runs; `node_modules/xrpl` is a symlink to `../../packages/xrpl`. Modules fund wallets
from the genesis account and must run one at a time.

`npm run probes` prints, for ~50 deliberately malformed MPT transactions, what the SDK's
`validate()` says next to what rippled's `simulate` says; rows marked `<-- SDK could catch` are the
validator gaps.
